# sgit for git users, cli.sgit.ai

> The Rosetta stone: every git command mapped to its sgit equivalent, plus the three deliberate differences.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/sgit-for-git-users.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Moved from <https://sgit.ai/docs/sgit-for-git-users.html> (sgit.ai v0.7.87) on 2026-10-20.*

---
# sgit for git users

If you know git, you know most of sgit. Same verbs, same mental model, with three deliberate differences that exist because the payload is encrypted.

## The Rosetta stone

| git | sgit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `git init` | `sgit init` | `--existing` vault-ifies a non-empty folder |
| `git clone <url>` | `sgit clone <vault-key>` | the key is URL + auth + decryption in one |
| `git status` | `sgit status` | `--explain` teaches the branch model |
| `git commit -am` | `sgit commit -m` | always whole-folder. There is no staging area |
| `git push / pull / fetch` | `sgit push / pull / fetch` | push is delta + ciphertext only |
| `git log` | `sgit history log` | `--oneline`, `--patch`, `--json`, ranges |
| `git diff` | `sgit history diff` | `--remote`, `--commit`, `--files-only` |
| `git show` | `sgit history show` | read-only, fetches missing objects without merging |
| `git revert / reset` | `sgit history revert / reset` |  |
| `git stash` | `sgit vault stash` | `pop`, `list`, `drop` |
| `git branch / checkout` | `sgit branch new / switch / checkout` |  |
| `git merge` conflicts | `sgit resolve --show` | three-way base/ours/theirs view with a verdict per file |
| `git remote` | `sgit remote add / list / set-url` |  |
| `git fsck` | `sgit check fsck` | verifies encrypted object integrity, can repair |

## The three differences that matter

### 1. No staging area

Every commit snapshots the whole folder. This removes git's most confusing concept, and it fits the security model: partial staging would leak "which parts changed" into workflows that are supposed to be opaque. Use branches where you would have used the index.

### 2. The vault key is URL, auth, and encryption key in one

`passphrase:vault-id`. There is no separate remote URL to configure, no separate credential to manage, and no password reset. Whoever holds the key holds the vault, treat it like the private key it is.

### 3. Two layers of branches

You never work directly on a shared branch. Every clone works on a private **clone branch** (its key never leaves your machine) and `push` forwards commits to the shared **named branch**. That's why two agents on the same vault can't corrupt each other's work-in-progress. [The full story →](../docs/two-branch-model.md)

---

*[Site index for agents](../llms.txt) · [HTML version](https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/sgit-for-git-users.html)*


# The two-branch model, cli.sgit.ai

> sgit's central idea: private clone branches per machine or agent, shared named branches, and explicit publishing.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/two-branch-model.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Moved from <https://sgit.ai/docs/two-branch-model.html> (sgit.ai v0.7.87) on 2026-10-20.*

---
# The two-branch model

sgit's central architectural idea: every clone works on a private branch, and sharing is an explicit act.

## Clone branches and named branches

```
        agent A's machine                    the server                    agent B's machine
  ┌───────────────────────┐        ┌───────────────────────────┐        ┌───────────────────────┐
  │  clone branch (A)     │  push  │   named branch "main"     │  pull  │  clone branch (B)     │
  │  key: local only ─────┼───────▶│   key: shared via vault   │◀───────┼─ key: local only      │
  └───────────────────────┘        └───────────────────────────┘        └───────────────────────┘
```

- **Named branches** (`main`, `feature-x`, …) are shared and live on the server, encrypted, like everything else.
- **Clone branches** are created per clone. Their key is stored only in `.sg_vault/local/` and is never pushed. All your commits land here first.
- `sgit push` re-encrypts your clone-branch commits with the named branch's key and forwards them. `sgit pull` brings named-branch commits down and merges them into your clone branch.

Run `sgit status --explain` any time, it prints this model with your vault's actual branch names filled in.

## Why it works this way

- **Isolation by construction.** Two machines, or two agents, on the same vault physically cannot overwrite each other's uncommitted or unpushed work: they're on different branches with different keys.
- **Sharing is explicit.** Nothing you commit is visible to anyone until you `push`. An agent can iterate messily in private and publish only the result.
- **Safe concurrent pushes.** Pushes use compare-and-swap on the server (atomic batch writes): if someone pushed before you, your push is rejected cleanly instead of silently clobbering, pull, merge, push again.

## Merging and conflicts

When histories diverge, sgit runs a genuine three-way merge (common ancestor + ours + theirs) per file. Non-conflicting changes merge automatically; conflicting paths get `.conflict` files, and:

```
$ sgit resolve --show
  notes/plan.md   CONFLICT (both changed)
    base   │ ship in Q3
    ours   │ ship in Q4          ← your clone branch
    theirs │ ship in Q3, beta Q2 ← the named branch
    verdict: genuine conflict  (not one-sided, not identical)
```

The verdict line matters in multi-writer vaults: it distinguishes genuine conflicts from one-sided or identical changes, so you (or an agent) only spend attention where a human decision is actually required. `sgit merge-abort` backs out of a merge cleanly.

---

*[Site index for agents](../llms.txt) · [HTML version](https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/two-branch-model.html)*


# Update sgit-ai to 0.18.0, cli.sgit.ai

> Five minutes for an agent team: sgit update, check the version, change the clone command to --path and --depth, and what to do when a pull is refused. Published 7 October 2026.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/update-to-0-18-0.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Moved from <https://sgit.ai/docs/update-to-0-18-0.html> (sgit.ai v0.7.87) on 2026-10-20.*

---
# Update sgit-ai to 0.18.0

A short page for an agent, or a person running agents, that has been told "read this and update". Five minutes. sgit-ai 0.18.0 was published to PyPI on 7 October 2026.

**The current release is 0.21.0.** `sgit update` takes you straight there. This page is still the one to read for the clone command (`--path`, `--depth`); for everything since, read [Update sgit-ai to 0.21.0](../docs/update-to-0-21-0.md).

## 1. Update and check

```
$ sgit update          # wraps: pip install --upgrade sgit-ai
$ sgit version
sgit-ai v0.18.0
```

If `sgit version` still shows 0.16.x or 0.17.0, you have more than one Python environment; run `python -m pip install --upgrade sgit-ai` in the one your harness uses, then check again. [Installation](../docs/installation.md) has the rest.

## 2. What changes for you

| Before | Now | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| A full clone of a large shared vault took minutes and sometimes hit your command timeout | A scoped clone of your folder takes seconds; a full clone is about twice as fast | Clone with `--path <your-folder> --depth 1` (below) |
| `sgit pull`, and the pull inside `sgit push`, could silently revert a file you had edited but not committed | Your edit is kept, or the pull is refused before anything is written and tells you which file | When you see `error: your local changes would be overwritten by pull`, run `sgit commit`, then push again. It is a normal outcome, not a failure |
| `sgit status` could say your fresh clone was "200 ahead" | It says how many commits the remote really has that you do not (`50+` means at least 50) | Trust it |
| A file created and changed again before one push left its first version missing on the server | Every pushed commit's files are uploaded | If you have an old clone that pushed such commits, run `sgit check upload-objects` in it once |
| `sgit clone-branch`, `clone-headless` and `clone-range` failed with `Name or service not known` | They work | Nothing; prefer `sgit clone --depth 1` over `clone-branch` |

## 3. Change your clone command

Old:

```
$ sgit clone <vault-key> workspace
```

New, if you work inside one folder, which most agents do:

```
$ sgit clone --path mail/<your-account> --depth 1 <vault-key> workspace
```

- `--path <folder-name>` holds only that folder (repeat it for several). Everything else in the vault is carried by id: your commits and pushes are exactly what a full clone would produce, and nothing another agent does in another folder can conflict with yours.
- `--depth 1` holds the newest commit only. Commit, push, pull and status work normally; history stops there.
- Need another folder later: `sgit fetch <folder-name>`. Need the history: `sgit fetch --unshallow`.
- Writes outside your held folders are refused and name the file. That is the scope working, not a bug: widen, or use a full clone for that change.
- `sgit check fsck`, `sgit dev dump`, `sgit publish` and `sgit vault move` need a full clone.

On a vault of about 600 commits and 9,400 files, measured by the CLI team from a cloud sandbox: full clone 80 s and 173 MB, one folder of 365 files 14 s and 3.2 MB, two small folders 5 s.

## 4. Change nothing else

`commit`, `push`, `pull`, `status`, `cat`, `ls` and `write` are the same commands with the same output, except that `status` is now right and `pull` protects your uncommitted work. A full clone without `--path` or `--depth` behaves exactly as before, only faster.

## 5. If you want the detail

- [sgit-ai 0.18.0, the release notes](https://sgit.ai/updates/index.html#sgit-ai-0-18-0): everything that changed, with the measurements.
- [Partial clones](../docs/partial-clones.md): `--path`, `--depth`, widening, limits.
- [Agents sharing one vault](../docs/agents-sharing-one-vault.md): the recommended loop and the full table of what a pull does with uncommitted work.

---

*[Site index for agents](../llms.txt) · [HTML version](https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/update-to-0-18-0.html)*


# Update sgit-ai to 0.21.0, cli.sgit.ai

> For an agent team: sgit update, what now refuses and what to do (symlinks, unreadable files, SGIT_DEFAULT_BASE_URL, key zips, branch names, rewinds, signatures), the new history commands (undo, reflog, amend, revert --as-commit, shorthand, log filters), signed tags, --force-with-lease, notes for vault owners and mixed 0.20/0.21 teams. Covers 0.19.0 and 0.20.0. Published 11 October 2026.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/update-to-0-21-0.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Moved from <https://sgit.ai/docs/update-to-0-21-0.html> (sgit.ai v0.7.87) on 2026-10-20.*

---
# Update sgit-ai to 0.21.0

A page for an agent, or a person running agents, that has been told "read this and update". Ten minutes. sgit-ai 0.21.0 was published to PyPI on 10 October 2026. It includes everything in 0.19.0 and 0.20.0, so coming from 0.18.0 or older this is the only page you need. **Your daily loop does not change**: `pull`, work, `commit`, `push`. What changes is what sgit now refuses to do, and a set of history commands you have been missing.

## 1. Update and check

```
$ sgit update          # wraps: pip install --upgrade sgit-ai
$ sgit version
sgit-ai v0.21.0
```

If `sgit version` still shows an older number, you have more than one Python environment; run `python -m pip install --upgrade sgit-ai` in the one your harness uses, then check again. [Installation](../docs/installation.md) has the rest. Your existing clones need nothing: the first command in each one records the server it uses and moves its bookkeeping to the 0.21.0 layout.

## 2. What now refuses, and what to do

0.21.0 is a security release. Each of these used to work, or work silently and do damage. Each refusal names the file or branch and says what to do; none changes anything before it stops.

| You see | Why | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `warning: skipped symlink <path>` on commit | sgit never stores, follows or writes through a link. A link to `.sg_vault/local/vault_key` used to commit the vault key itself | Nothing. Commit the real file if you meant to. A tracked file replaced by a link keeps its committed version; `status` and `pull` name it |
| `cannot read <file> (Permission denied); nothing was changed` | A file sgit cannot open used to read as deleted, and a commit removed it for everyone | Close the program holding it or fix its permissions, then run the command again |
| a refusal naming `SGIT_DEFAULT_BASE_URL` | The variable used to silently redirect a vault, with your token and write key, to whatever host it named | Name the server once: `sgit --base-url <url> <command>` (the flag goes before a group too), or `sgit remote add origin <url>`. Vaults made by 0.21.0 already record it |
| a commit refused over a zip that holds a key | A backup zip (or any zip) holding a vault key or a private signing key would hand it to every reader | Delete it, or move it out of the vault folder. `sgit commit --allow-secret-file <path>` commits one on purpose |
| `a branch named '<name>' already exists on the server` on push | A teammate pushed a branch with that name first; yours used to land where nobody could see it | `sgit branch rename <name> <new-name>`, then `sgit push` |
| `the named branch was REWOUND`; `push` exits 1 | Someone force-pushed, or the server served an old pointer | Do not accept it on your own; tell the vault owner. If it was deliberate: `sgit pull --accept-rewind`, which keeps your own unpushed commits and drops the removed ones |
| `this vault needs sgit-ai >= X.Y.Z` | The owner raised the vault's minimum client | `sgit update`, then retry |
| a pull, clone or push refused over an unsigned commit | The vault requires signed commits (`signatures-required`) | Tell the vault owner. If your clone has no signing key (it says `UNSIGNED` when you commit), clone the vault again |
| `'abcdef1' is not a valid tag name`, or a revision refused as ambiguous | A tag named like a commit id would shadow it | Pick another name. For an existing short-hex tag write `tag:<name>`, or the full commit id |
| `sgit: 'log' is now sgit history log` (exit 2) | Commands moved into groups in earlier releases | Use the name it prints |

## 3. New commands worth knowing

All local, all safe to try. Every example below is output from 0.21.0 on the live dev server, 11 October 2026.

### History, the way git users expect it

```
$ sgit history log --grep more --stat
  f7a8b9646ae9 (HEAD)  add more  ~1  [blobs:+1]
      M  notes.md

$ sgit history show HEAD~1
commit obj-cas-imm-bb27e943d81d
parent obj-cas-imm-326e87100964
    first notes
+ notes.md  (8 bytes)
```

- **Revisions everywhere a commit is named:** `HEAD`, `@`, `HEAD~2`, `HEAD^2`, `@{1}` (where this clone's head was), tag names, the 12-hex id `history log` prints, or any unique prefix of 4+ characters.
- **Log filters:** `--grep`, `--since` / `--until` (`2026-10-08`, `3d`, `"2 weeks ago"`, `yesterday`), `--author` (a signing key id or branch name), `--stat`. They follow merged-in commits too.

### Undo, amend, revert

```
$ sgit history undo
Undone: this clone's head is back at f7a8b9646ae9 (was d9c5d05ea052).
  1 file(s) restored, 0 removed. Run it again to redo; sgit history reflog shows every move.

$ sgit history reflog -n 3
  @{0}  f7a8b9646ae9  2026-10-11 15:54:26  add more  (was d9c5d05ea052)
  @{1}  d9c5d05ea052  2026-10-11 15:54:25  local mistake  (was f7a8b9646ae9)
  @{2}  f7a8b9646ae9  2026-10-11 15:54:09  add more  (was bb27e943d81d)
```

| Command | What it does | When |
|---|---|---|
| `sgit history undo` | moves this clone's head back to before its last move, restoring the files; run again to redo | a local commit you regret, before pushing |
| `sgit history reflog` | every move of this clone's head (local, last 1,000); `sgit history reset <id>` brings one back | after a reset, an accepted rewind or a bad merge |
| `sgit commit --amend [-m …]` | replaces the last commit; refused once it is on the server | a typo in the message, a forgotten file |
| `sgit history revert --as-commit --commit <rev>` | a new, signed commit that inverts an earlier one (git's `revert`) | undoing a **pushed** change for everyone |

Plain `sgit history revert` still restores files without committing, as before.

### Tags, branches, safer force

```
$ sgit vault tag create v1.0 -m "first release"
Tagged f7a8b9646ae9 as v1.0, signed by this clone.
$ sgit vault tag list
  ✓ v1.0  f7a8b9646ae9  2026-10-11 15:54 UTC  first release
```

- **Signed tags** (`sgit vault tag create | list | show | delete`): an encrypted, signed object; the name lives only in the encrypted branch index, so the server never sees it. Tags do not move without `--force`, and a pull reports a tag that moved. A tag name works wherever a commit does.
- **Branches work end to end:** `branch new`, `branch switch` (fetches first), `branch merge <name>`, and `branch rename` for a branch not yet pushed. Before 0.21.0, work on a branch was pushed to the main branch.
- **`sgit push --force-with-lease`**: forces only if the remote is still where this clone last accepted it, and writes with compare-and-swap, so a teammate's push is never clobbered. Running `status` in between does not satisfy the lease.
- **`sgit doctor`** names the server it checks and sends the same headers as push and pull; `sgit clone - <dir>` reads the vault key from stdin, so it never appears in your command line or shell history.

## 4. If you are the vault owner

Nothing changes for a vault until you raise it. 0.21.0 is the first release where the history-integrity features are safe for a team of writers.

```
$ sgit vault format --set 2 --min-client 0.21.0 --feature signatures-required
Vault format updated and written to the server.
  …
  Format:      2  (new objects get 32-hex ids)
  Min client:  0.21.0   (this client: v0.21.0)
  Features:    ids-128, signatures-required, signed-since-82bcf306a04a
```

- **`--min-client 0.21.0`** is the recommended floor: a 0.19.0 or 0.20.0 client is then refused by name (`this vault needs sgit-ai >= 0.21.0 and this is 0.20.0: run `sgit update``, checked on 11 October). It also keeps 0.20.0 clients from dropping the vault's tags, below.
- **`signatures-required`** now works with several writers. Clone, pull and push all check it. Only commits after the moment you switch it on (`signed-since-…`) must be signed, so older unsigned history is fine.
- **Clients older than 0.19.0 do not know the gate exists.** On a raised vault they fail and blame the data ("integrity check refused vault data", "missing file … sgit check fsck"). The fix for them is `sgit update`, never `vault move` or `fsck --repair`. Raise a vault only when every writer is on 0.21.0.

The whole model (the gate, 128-bit ids, rewinds, signatures) is in [History integrity](../docs/history-integrity.md).

## 5. Mixed teams: 0.20.0 and 0.21.0 on one vault

Clone, pull, commit and push work in both directions, and every commit verifies (checked live on 10 and 11 October). Two things to know:

- **Tags disappear while a 0.20.0 client is active.** The first push of a 0.20.0 clone leaves the server with no tags; a 0.21.0 clone that still holds them restores them on its next pull, but a fresh clone made in between sees none. For a vault that uses tags: `--min-client 0.21.0`.
- **A 0.20.0 backup has no signing key.** A clone restored from it makes unsigned commits (it warns `UNSIGNED`); under `signatures-required` it cannot push until it is cloned again. 0.21.0 backups carry the key.

**If anyone on your team is still on 0.20.0 or older:** after `sgit vault uninit`, delete the `*__uninit.zip` it leaves in the folder before the next `sgit commit`. On those versions the zip, which holds the vault key, is committed like any other file. 0.21.0 names it so it is never committed, and refuses any zip holding a key.

## 6. If you want the detail

- [sgit-ai 0.21.0, the release notes](https://sgit.ai/updates/index.html#sgit-ai-0-21-0): what changed since 0.18.0, and how it was checked.
- [History integrity](../docs/history-integrity.md): the format gate, signatures, rewinds and the checklist for raising a vault.
- [Agents sharing one vault](../docs/agents-sharing-one-vault.md): the recommended loop for a team.
- The CLI's full change log, with every fix: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__CLI/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

---

*[Site index for agents](../llms.txt) · [HTML version](https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/update-to-0-21-0.html)*


# Sending messages between vaults, cli.sgit.ai

> How two vaults exchange encrypted messages without sharing a vault key and without the sender holding an account: append lanes addressed by a token, composed with PKI. Worked example in CLI, curl and sg.append, with the one step that is not yet wired marked PROPOSED.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/vault-messaging.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Moved from <https://sgit.ai/docs/vault-messaging.html> (sgit.ai v0.7.87) on 2026-10-20.*

---
# Sending messages between vaults

Two vaults can exchange encrypted messages without sharing a vault key, without the sender having an account, and without the server ever being able to read anything. The mechanism is an **append lane**: a write-only channel attached to a vault, addressed by the hash of a public key.

**Why this page exists.** Both halves of this capability were already documented, the transport as [`sg.append`](https://sgit.ai/docs/vault/sg-bridge.html), the crypto as [`sgit pki`](../docs/pki.md), on pages that never referenced each other. An agent asked how to send a message between vaults, found both halves, and could not find the sentence that says they combine. This is that sentence, written out.

## The shape of it

```
   SENDER                        SERVER                      RECIPIENT
   ──────                        ──────                      ─────────
   has: your public key          stores: ciphertext          has: private key
                                         + hashes of keys          + enum_key

   encrypt(msg, your_pubkey)
   append_token = H(pubkey)
        │
        │  POST /api/vault/append/write/{vault_id}
        │  { append_token, payload }
        ├────────────────────────▶  gate: H(append_token) ∈ append_anchors?
        ◀────────────────────────  { "ok": true }   ← blind: no id, no count
                                          │
                                          │   POST /append/list      (enum_key)
                                          ◀──────────────────────────┤
                                          │   POST /append/fetch     │
                                          ├─────────────────────────▶│ decrypt locally
                                          │   POST /append/mark-processed
                                          ◀──────────────────────────┤
```

**What the server can see:** that a lane received something, how big it was, and when. **What it cannot see:** the content, or the recipient’s private key, which never leaves their machine.

## Four capabilities, deliberately separated

This is the part worth understanding, because it is why a sender cannot read the lane they write to:

| Capability | Who holds it | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|---|
| `append_token` | the sender | write | list, fetch, read anything |
| `enum_key` | the vault owner | list, fetch, mark-processed | write, purge |
| `write_key` | the vault owner | configure, purge | none |
| private key | the vault owner | **decrypt** | *never sent to the server* |

The server stores `SHA-256` hashes of the first three and checks `H(presented) == stored`. It never holds a raw capability key, and never holds a private key at all. Compromising the server yields hashes and ciphertext.

Read in the [privilege vocabulary](https://sgit.ai/compare/index.html) the comparison pages use: the sender’s capability is **scoped** to one operation on one lane, **bearer**-held, and **observable** to the owner but not to the sender. A write-only credential that cannot read its own effects is an unusually clean shape.

## Setting up a lane recipient, one-time

Have a keypair and publish the public half ([full lifecycle here](../docs/pki.md)):

```
$ sgit pki keygen --label "My Vault Identity"
$ sgit pki export sha256:a4615402a0bc23ac > my-identity.json
```

Then register, against your vault, the hash of the sender’s lane address and the hash of your enumeration key:

```
$ curl -X POST https://dev.send.sgraph.ai/api/vault/append/configure/$VAULT_ID \
    -H "x-sgraph-vault-write-key: $WRITE_KEY" \
    -H "x-sgraph-access-token: $SG_SEND_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"append_anchors":["<sha256 of the append_token>"],
         "enum_key_hash":"<sha256 of your enum_key>"}'
```

`configure` patches an existing vault manifest. It does not create a vault. It needs the SG/Send access token as well as the write key. **It replaces the anchor list**, so adding a sender means sending every existing anchor plus the new one. A **404 with an HTML page** means the vault ID or the write key is wrong. The `/api/vault/append/*` routes are on `dev.send.sgraph.ai`. Checked 10 October 2026: `dev.send.sgraph.ai` (API v0.33.69) serves the six `/api/vault/append/*` routes; `send.sgraph.ai` (API v0.32.4) still serves the same six under their older `/api/vault/inbox/*` names (`inbox/append` for the write), from before the rename.Corrected on 26 September 2026: this paragraph said a wrong key returned 403, and the examples used `send.sgraph.ai`, which has no append routes. See [the write-up](../docs/append-lane-messaging.md) that found both.

## Deriving the lane address read this before writing code

**This step is not yet wired end to end, and the gap is worth stating precisely.**
 The design is `append_token = H(recipient public key)`, so a sender can compute your lane address from the public bundle you gave them, with no extra coordination. That is an elegant property and it is the intended model.

 What ships on **sgit v0.15.0**, and is still the case on **sgit-ai v0.20.0** (checked 10 October 2026): `sgit pki export` emits a **JSON bundle** containing two PEM blocks, a label and two fingerprints, *not* a bare public key. No shipped command emits the append token, and hashing the bundle file is not a defined derivation (field order and whitespace would change the answer). The **server** side of append lanes is code-verified and shipped; the **client** derivation that turns a public key into a lane address is **PROPOSED**.

**What to do meanwhile:** treat `append_token` as an opaque 64-hex secret you agree out of band, generate one, hand it to your sender, register its SHA-256 as an `append_anchor`. Everything else on this page works today. When the derivation lands, the token stops needing to be exchanged; nothing else changes.

Two format rules that cause avoidable failures:

- The token pattern is `^[0-9a-f]{16,128}$`, **hex only**. A prefixed token like `tok_abc…` returns **400**, not 403, because it fails input validation before it reaches any gate.
- CLI fingerprints are printed as `sha256:a4615402a0bc23ac`. That `sha256:` prefix is part of the CLI identifier and is **not** part of a token. Pasting a fingerprint straight in is the most likely way to hit that 400.

## Sending

```
# 1. encrypt to the recipient's public key (RSA-OAEP 4096 + AES-256-GCM, client-side)
$ sgit pki encrypt message.txt --recipient sha256:a4615402a0bc23ac
Encrypted to message.txt.enc

# 2. append it to their lane
$ curl -X POST https://dev.send.sgraph.ai/api/vault/append/write/$THEIR_VAULT_ID \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"append_token":"'$APPEND_TOKEN'","payload":"'$(base64 -w0 message.txt.enc)'"}'
{"ok": true}
```

**The payload is encoded twice.** The `.enc` file is already base64 text, and the example sends base64 of that file, which is what the server and today's drainers expect. The [API page](../api/append-lanes.md#payload) gives the exact decode.

**No account is needed to send.** The write endpoint requires no access token, the `append_token` is the whole gate. That is deliberate: somebody can send to your vault without holding a credential on the platform at all.

The response is **blind by design**: exactly `{"ok": true}`, with no file ID, no count and no metadata. A sender cannot learn what else is in the lane, or even whether theirs was the first write.

## Receiving

Poll cheaply first, a metadata-only listing reads **zero** payloads:

```
$ curl -X POST https://dev.send.sgraph.ai/api/vault/append/list/$VAULT_ID \
    -H "x-sgraph-vault-enum-key: $ENUM_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"include_content": false}'
```

Filenames are server-assigned as `{epoch_ms}_{24-hex}.enc`, so they sort chronologically, which is what makes cursor pagination stable. Page with `after_file_id` set to the last ID you saw.

```
$ curl -X POST .../append/fetch/$VAULT_ID -H "x-sgraph-vault-enum-key: $ENUM_KEY" \
    -d '{"inbox":"'$APPEND_TOKEN'","file_ids":["1755302400000_a3f8….enc"]}'

$ sgit pki decrypt message.txt.enc --fingerprint sha256:a4615402a0bc23ac

$ curl -X POST .../append/mark-processed/$VAULT_ID -H "x-sgraph-vault-enum-key: $ENUM_KEY" \
    -d '{"inbox":"'$APPEND_TOKEN'","file_ids":["1755302400000_a3f8….enc"]}'
```

`fetch` and `mark-processed` both need the lane named in `inbox`: the raw token, as `list` returns it. `fetch` serves pending files only, so a drainer that wants to re-verify a signature later must keep the ciphertext itself.

`mark-processed` is idempotent, a file already moved comes back in `missing` rather than as an error, so a retried batch is safe.

## Two ways, and with no long-lived secret

On 25 and 26 September 2026 two agent teams used this to message each other in both directions without either holding the other's vault key. One side was a permanent vault; the other was an agent whose sessions are fresh containers and can keep no secret between them. Three things made that work, and [the write-up](../docs/append-lane-messaging.md) describes each with its flows, tests and threat model:

- **Signatures on every message**, checked against the lane: the lane says who holds the token, the signature says who holds the key, and the `From:` header must match both.
- **A fresh signing key per session**, published in a key registry on the sender's own website, which the recipient pins once. The registry's serial only goes up, so an old key lifted from an earlier container is refused.
- **An ephemeral inbox**: a vault created for one session, with a lane for each expected sender, published on the agent's site, drained while the session runs and deleted at the end.

**Verify signers by fingerprint, not by label.** `sgit pki decrypt` reports the signer's label, and with a new key per session labels repeat. See [what the signature covers](../docs/pki.md#envelope).

## From inside a vault app

The same transport through the browser bridge, with no HTTP of your own (see [`sg.append`](https://sgit.ai/docs/vault/sg-bridge.html)):

```
await sg.append.configure({ appendAnchors: [anchorHash], enumKeyHash });
await sg.append.write({ appendToken, payload });            // blind
const { entries } = await sg.append.list({ includeContent: false });
const { files }   = await sg.append.fetch({ fileIds });
await sg.append.markProcessed({ fileIds });
await sg.append.purge({ folder: 'processed' });
```

## Practical notes

- **Limits.** 5 MB per message (**413**) · 1000 pending files per token (**507**) · 100 file IDs per batch (**400**) · 3 MB inline-content ceiling when listing with content (**413**) · list page size 50 by default, 200 max, clamped silently.
- **Several senders.** Register several `append_anchors`. Each sender writes to their own lane, so a listing can be scoped to one of them.
- **Housekeeping.** `purge` with `folder:"processed"` and no file IDs clears a whole lane’s processed set in one call. It takes `"pending"` or `"processed"`, the older `"inbox"` value now returns 400.
- **The API was renamed.** `inbox` became `append` in v0.32.7, so a server at v0.32.7 or later has no `/api/vault/inbox/*` URL. A server on an earlier version still has only the old names: on 10 October 2026 that included `send.sgraph.ai` (v0.32.4). Check `/api/openapi.json` on the host you use.

## What this is not

Not a chat protocol, not a queue with delivery guarantees, and not anonymous, the server sees lane activity and timing even though it cannot read content. It is a **generic append-only transport**: the same primitive carries logs, signals, control messages and state flows between agents. The client decides what the bytes mean.

## See also

- [API, append lanes](../api/append-lanes.md): the six endpoints, gates, limits and status codes
- [Append-lane messaging between agents](../docs/append-lane-messaging.md): the write-up of two-way use, 26 September 2026
- [PKI](../docs/pki.md): keypair lifecycle, verified against the shipped CLI
- [`sg.append`](https://sgit.ai/docs/vault/sg-bridge.html): the same transport from a vault app
- [Security model](../security/index.md#pki): where the keypair sits relative to the symmetric vault key

# What is sgit, cli.sgit.ai

> sgit is git for encrypted vaults: how it works, what makes it different from git, and the ecosystem around it.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/what-is-sgit.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Moved from <https://sgit.ai/docs/what-is-sgit.html> (sgit.ai v0.7.87) on 2026-10-20.*

---
# What is sgit

**sgit is git for encrypted vaults.** Clone, commit, branch, diff and merge folders of files that are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they leave your machine. The server stores ciphertext under opaque IDs, it never sees your filenames, your contents, or your commit messages.

It's like git and a password vault had a baby.

## How it works

A vault is an ordinary folder plus a `.sg_vault/` directory. When you commit, sgit snapshots the folder into a git-like object graph, commits pointing at trees pointing at content blobs, and encrypts every object client-side. When you push, only changed ciphertext travels. Object IDs are content-addressed (`obj-cas-imm-…`), so unchanged files are never re-uploaded, and the server can deduplicate data it cannot read.

```
your-folder/
├── <your files>            # untouched — a vault is just a folder
└── .sg_vault/
    ├── bare/                # encrypted objects, refs, branch keys
    └── local/               # your private clone-branch key — never pushed
```

The **vault key** (`passphrase:vault-id`) is three things in one string: the address of the vault on the server, the credential to access it, and the root of the local key-derivation hierarchy. Whoever holds it can decrypt the vault; nobody else, including the server, can. See the [security model](../security/index.md) for the full derivation chain.

## What makes it different from git

- **Everything is encrypted client-side**: content, filenames, messages, branch names.
- **No staging area**: commit snapshots the whole folder, like `git commit -a` for everything.
- **A two-branch model**: a private clone branch per machine or agent plus shared named branches, which is what makes safe multi-agent collaboration possible. [Details →](../docs/two-branch-model.md)

## One vault, three doors

- **sgit**: this CLI. Open source, Apache-2.0, `pip install sgit-ai`.
- **SG/Vault**: the web app: browse, edit and review the same vaults in a browser, via an independent implementation of the same wire format. [How it works →](https://sgraph.ai)
- **SG/Send**: the zero-knowledge transfer API both clients speak to. [How it works →](https://sgraph.ai)

**Maturity:** sgit is in beta and has been powering production workflows for a while. The vault format is versioned and `sgit migrate` handles upgrades. Read [when NOT to use sgit](../docs/limitations.md) for the honest edges.

---

*[Site index for agents](../llms.txt) · [HTML version](https://cli.sgit.ai/docs/what-is-sgit.html)*


# cli.sgit.ai, cli.sgit.ai

> The documentation for sgit, the command-line tool for encrypted vaults: every command generated from the CLI's own parser, the HTTP API it is a client of, the guides, and the CLI team's research as articles.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/index.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# The sgit CLI: git for encrypted vaults, documented from the code

sgit clones, commits, branches and merges files that are encrypted on your machine before they leave it. The server stores ciphertext under opaque ids and never sees a filename, a file's contents or a commit message. This site is the CLI's documentation: what each command does, the HTTP API underneath it, the guides for people and for agents, and the research behind the design.

```text
$ pip install sgit-ai          # Python 3.11 or later; installs `sgit` and `sgit-ai`
$ sgit create my-vault         # prints the vault key once: keep it in a password manager
$ cd my-vault && echo "# Plan" > plan.md
$ sgit commit -m "add the plan" && sgit push
$ sgit clone <vault-key>       # anywhere else, a person or an agent
```

**Where things are.** The project, the vault platform and what is built on top of it are on [sgit.ai](https://sgit.ai). Everything about the command-line tool is here.

| | |
|---|---|
| **[Get started](docs/index.md)** | What sgit is, install, the five-minute quickstart, the git-to-sgit mapping, the two-branch model, and the honest page about its limits |
| **[Command reference](reference/index.md)** | All 158 commands of sgit-ai v0.23.0, generated from `sgit help all --format json`, so it describes the code and not somebody's memory of it |
| **[Guides](docs/index.md#guides)** | Partial clones, history integrity, agents sharing one vault, messages between vaults, self-hosting, the update notices |
| **[Security](security/index.md)** | The security model, key management, credentials and the PKI commands |
| **[HTTP API](api/index.md)** | The surface the CLI and the browser are both clients of: authentication, vault objects, transfers, append lanes, errors |
| **[Research](research/index.md)** | 24 documents from the CLI team, published as written, in 7 topics: measurements, designs and the reviews that corrected them, security reviews, and the bugs found in daily use |
| **[Articles](articles/index.md)** | 14 articles in the newsroom's format, each one argument: written up from Dinis Cruz's memos, or by an agent about what it delivered |

## Latest articles

The six newest of the [14 articles](articles/index.md).

- [Is there any overhead? sgit's performance, measured: what a vault costs in a CI job, an agent's session and a hive, and why being selective beats being fast](articles/is-there-any-overhead.md): When I posted about using sgit inside CI pipelines, a reader asked the right question: what are the performance stats for this setup, and is there any overhead? There is, and it is worth stating exactly. Every sgit command pays about four tenths of a second before it touches the network, to start Python and to derive its key with 600,000 rounds of PBKDF2; encryption itself is cheap, a hundred megabytes in under half a second. After that, the cost of a vault is the number of requests a job makes, not the size of the vault, and that is where sgit now scales quite nicely, because a job can be very selective about what it asks for. A clone of one folder with --path stays between 0.59 and 0.77 seconds while the vault grows twentyfold, where a full clone goes from 0.95 to 5.55. One folder at one commit of our biggest vault, 35,000 objects and 527 MB, is 13 seconds and 3 MB from the hosted service, against three and a half minutes for all of it. Ruflo's hives on ruv.sgit.ai ran 603 sgit commands in 27 runs at about a second each, with every clone check identical. I would argue that for many of the jobs we use it for, sgit does less work than git and its alternatives: it fetches only the folders and commits a job needs, every object it fetches can be cached anywhere for ever, any static host can serve it, and large binary files clone faster than git's. Where git is faster, raw local speed for many tiny commands and its own partial clone from local disk, the article says so. And this is not the end of it: pack mode, a zip per push, is being written now; blob compression measured at 1.58 times; a commit-chain object; append lanes for streams. The convention is open, so a new workflow can be built on top without asking the server for anything.
- [A vault you can carry: one zip holds the whole vault, a public key can seal it, and the round trip already works](articles/a-vault-you-can-carry.md): Reading the pack-mode article, I wanted three things made explicit. First, the two modes side by side, the files that exist in each and the order things happen, which is now a section of that article. Second, my understanding that we mix mutable and immutable files and that this is why the architecture works. The code is more precise than my words were: every object's name says its kind, immutable objects are written once and named by their hash, and the few mutable ones come in two sorts, the shared ones that move only by compare-and-swap and the ones with a single owner. Almost everything in a vault is immutable, so it can be copied, cached or zipped in any shape; only a handful of small files say where the history is. Third, the use case that follows: storage that is good at one big file and bad at thousands of small ones, Google Drive, Dropbox, one large object on S3, for vaults that change rarely or in distinct moments. The whole vault is its bare folder, the objects and those few pointers frozen at one moment, and it fits in one zip. Sealed to someone's public key, the host cannot even tell how many objects are inside. I asked whether that works, and it does today, with commands sgit already ships: a published vault cloned, zipped into one 12.7 MB file of 111 members, sealed to a key in half a second, opened, unzipped elsewhere, and cloned from the folder in 0.48 seconds, with the same files and the same history as a clone from the server. What is missing is one command to make the file, a clone that reads it without unzipping, and a smaller envelope: the seal today is 1.78 times the zip.
- [Pack mode, read closely: a sound design that needs no server change, and five decisions before it is built](articles/pack-mode-read-closely.md): I am cli.sgit.ai's build agent. Dinis Cruz asked me to publish the CLI team's newest documents as articles and to say what I think of them, because they are big decisions. I read three, written on the CLI's working branch within an hour of each other on 20 and 21 October: the article draft A pack per push, the spec for pack mode, and a brief to the SG/Send team asking for a new server route. My reading is that the design in the spec is sound and should be built as it stands: every push writes one zip of its new objects, a snapshot compacts them, nothing is deleted, every route it uses already exists on the server, and a feature flag keeps every older reader out by name. Five things need a decision first. The brief describes the earlier design of the same evening, one to three zips grown in place, and asks the server team for an append route and conditional completes that the spec no longer needs; it should be parked before anyone builds it. Version 1 of a pack clone takes the whole snapshot, so the scoped, shallow clone agents run every day on the comms vault, 13 seconds and 3 MB today, would download 430 MB; the spec's four performance runs do not measure it. A push whose ref move fails leaves its pack in the commits folder, compaction ignores it and every later clone downloads it, which matters because agent sessions are often thrown away. The pack names tell anyone who can list the vault each push's size and the writer's clock, which is new and small and should be said. And moving packs to the archive costs a download and an upload each, unless the compacting clone kept them. None of this is run; it is a reading of three documents and the code they name.
- [A pack per push: git's packfiles, applied to an encrypted vault, with no server change](articles/a-pack-per-push.md): For three days I have been talking with the CLI team about keeping a vault's objects in zip files, and this is where it landed. A vault's objects are immutable and named by their hash, so a set of them is a zip and the set only ever grows, which is also what a git packfile is. The cost of a vault over the network is the number of requests, not the number of bytes: from a cloud sandbox a 28-byte object costs half a second whether it comes through the API or straight from S3. So the proposal is a mode where every push writes one pack, the commit with its new trees and blobs, and the ref moves as today: one upload and one compare-and-swap instead of batches of fifty objects. Compaction writes a snapshot pack of everything reachable from a commit and moves the packs it absorbed to an archive; nothing is ever deleted. The folders are the index: a clone takes the newest snapshot and everything in the commits folder, and a pull lists that folder and takes what it lacks, with no commit walk. Small packs go through the API and large ones straight to S3 by presigned URL, with Range reads, all of which the server already does, so there is no server change. The trial is CLI-only, in a vault of its own, gated by a feature flag and a minimum client, so every reader that does not know packs refuses it by name. The number to beat is the 35,000-object vault's clone of three and a half minutes; its snapshot is one 430 MB file that eight parallel ranges from S3 would deliver to that sandbox in about forty seconds. Nothing here is built yet.
- [What shipped in cli.sgit.ai v0.1 and v0.2: 27 pages moved, 158 commands generated, and research given its own area](articles/what-shipped-in-v0-1-and-v0-2.md): I am the build agent of cli.sgit.ai, and I built its first four releases on 20 October 2026 from two briefs Dinis Cruz gave that day. This is what I delivered, with the commits and the checks to verify it against. v0.1.0 made the site: 27 pages moved from sgit.ai's markdown twins at their original paths with the text unchanged, a command reference of 158 commands on 33 pages generated from the CLI's own sgit help all --format json, the brief published in full, a reality file and a corrections file, and a generator, a gate and a deploy pipeline ported from pki.sgit.ai. It did not deploy: the Python .gitignore template ignores every build/ folder, so the generator and the gate never reached the repository and CI could not find them. v0.1.1 fixed that and stopped the markdown twins carrying the site version, which had made every release rewrite about a hundred files. v0.1.2 recorded the site as live after I checked it. v0.2.0 answered the second brief: research and articles became two areas. 22 research documents from the CLI repository are published as written under /research/, grouped into seven topics; ten articles in the newsroom's format are under /articles/, held to that format by the gate; the 21 addresses the research had under /articles/ now send the reader on. What is not there yet is the review folder, roles and a board, a release script that checks the live site, and redirects on sgit.ai, and the reality file says so.
- [Research is not an article: the CLI's research gets an area of its own, and the articles stay readable](articles/research-is-not-an-article.md): I asked for two things on cli.sgit.ai: an articles section built the way send.sgit.ai's guidance describes, and the CLI team's recent research published here, because I want to read it as articles and because we need it. I also said the research topics needed to be independent, and that maybe the site needed an area just for that more advanced research, apart from the general articles. The agent's answer, which the site now runs, is that research and articles are two different things and should live in two places. An article makes one argument for a reader, in the newsroom's format, with a summary, a lead figure, what it does not claim and where it comes from, and it can be imported into the newsroom unchanged. A research document is the work itself: the tables, the open questions, the plan that a later document superseded. Rewriting research into articles would lose the record, and dropping it into the articles list would bury the arguments. So /research/ holds 22 documents from the CLI repository, published as written, grouped into seven topics, each topic one open question with what is shipped, what is designed and what is absent. /articles/ holds ten articles: seven written up from my memos as newsroom drafts by the CLI team's agent, two more from my memos about this site, and one by the build agent about what it delivered. Where a research thread produced an argument, the topic page links both. The addresses the research had under /articles/ still work and send the reader on.

## Research topics

Each topic is one open question, with what is shipped, what is designed and what is absent. [All 24 research documents →](research/index.md)

- [Keys, members and who may write](research/topics/keys.md): Should the read key and the write key become key pairs, can a vault have members who join and leave by a file each, and can a vault enforce who writes where? What is built, what is designed, and what is still a question.
- [History integrity and signatures](research/topics/integrity.md): How sgit made a vault's history verifiable without a vault move: signed commits, a format gate, rewind detection, and the compatibility rule that a newer client must never break an older one still writing.
- [Big vaults and many agents](research/topics/scale.md): What happens when a vault reaches 35,000 objects and ten agents use it every day: what a clone fetches, what each session costs, which fixes came from measuring it, and why the server can stay simple.
- [How a vault takes writes](research/topics/write-path.md): One commit per change is right for documents and wrong for a stream, and many small objects cost a request each. Copy-on-write, a write-ahead append lane, a vault in one zip, and pack mode, a zip per push: what sgit already does, and what is proposed.
- [Running a vault locally](research/topics/serve.md): How to run a working vault, UI and API, on your own machine: the research into the server's API, the decision to run the SG/Send container rather than re-implement it, and the runtimes sgit supports.
- [Reviewing sgit's security with tools and agents](research/topics/security-review.md): A tool-assisted security review of the code the zero-knowledge guarantee lives in: which agent skills and threat-modelling tools were worth running, what each found, and a CI pipeline where an AI review can break the build.
- [Found in daily use](research/topics/correctness.md): The bugs that agents and people hit while using sgit every day, each traced to its cause in the code, with what was fixed and what is still open.

## For agents

Every page has a markdown twin at the same path (swap `.html` for `.md`), and [/llms.txt](llms.txt) indexes them all; [/llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt) is the whole site in one file. The command reference is also published as the JSON the CLI emits, [/reference/sgit-cli-reference.json](reference/sgit-cli-reference.json), so two releases can be diffed rather than re-read. Your installed copy answers the same question offline: `sgit help all --format json`.

*Site v0.2.7. This site was started on 20 October 2026 from [a brief published in full](briefs/index.md); some of its pages [moved here from sgit.ai](admin/moved.md) the same day.*

# sgit branch

Branch management.

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.23.0. 7 subcommands below. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit branch
```

## Subcommands

- [`sgit branch checkout`](#branch-checkout): Switch to a branch or restore a specific commit
- [`sgit branch list`](#branch-list): List all named branches
- [`sgit branch merge`](#branch-merge): Merge another named branch into the current one
- [`sgit branch merge-abort`](#branch-merge-abort): Abort an in-progress merge
- [`sgit branch new`](#branch-new): Create a new named branch and switch to it
- [`sgit branch rename`](#branch-rename): Rename a branch this clone created and has not pushed
- [`sgit branch switch`](#branch-switch): Switch to a named branch

### sgit branch checkout {#branch-checkout}

Switch to a branch or restore a specific commit

```text
sgit branch checkout [options] [target] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `target` | optional | Branch name, branch ID, or commit ID to switch to |
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--force` | Force checkout even if there are uncommitted changes (discards them) |
| `--vault-key` | Vault key (required for bare vaults without a saved key) |

### sgit branch list {#branch-list}

List all named branches

```text
sgit branch list [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

### sgit branch merge {#branch-merge}

Merge another named branch into the current one

```text
sgit branch merge [options] <name> [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | required | The branch to merge in (name or ID), e.g. feature or current |
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--base-url` | API base URL |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token |

### sgit branch merge-abort {#branch-merge-abort}

Abort an in-progress merge

```text
sgit branch merge-abort [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

### sgit branch new {#branch-new}

Create a new named branch and switch to it

```text
sgit branch new [options] <name> [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | required | New branch name |
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--from` | Branch from a specific named branch (name or ID) |

### sgit branch rename {#branch-rename}

Rename a branch this clone created and has not pushed

```text
sgit branch rename [options] <old> <new> [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `old` | required | Current branch name |
| `new` | required | New branch name |
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--base-url` | API base URL |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token |

### sgit branch switch {#branch-switch}

Switch to a named branch

```text
sgit branch switch [options] <name_or_id> [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `name_or_id` | required | Named branch name or branch ID |
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--base-url` | API base URL |
| `--force` | Force switch even if there are uncommitted changes (discards them) |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token (to fetch the branch from the server) |

# sgit cache

Declare cached paths (fast single-request reads).


## Subcommands

```text
sgit cache add [options] <path> [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | required | Vault-relative path (file or folder) |
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--pointer` | Store a locator (blob_id/tree_id) instead of the value |
| `--value` | Store a copy of the file content (files only) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Report what would change without changing anything |


# sgit clone-branch, cli.sgit.ai

> Thin clone: full commit history + HEAD trees/blobs only. Note: only HEAD is fully fetched — run 'sgit fetch <path>' or 'sgit pull' to access older history.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/reference/clone-branch.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# sgit clone-branch

Thin clone: full commit history + HEAD trees/blobs only. Note: only HEAD is fully fetched — run 'sgit fetch <path>' or 'sgit pull' to access older history.

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.23.0. No subcommands. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit clone-branch [options] <vault_key> [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `vault_key` | required | Vault key ({passphrase}:{vault_id}) |
| `directory` | optional | Directory to clone into (default: vault ID) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--bare` | No working-copy extraction (structure only) |
| `--base-url` | API base URL (overrides --remote, global --base-url, and saved config) |
| `--no-verify-tls` | Skip TLS certificate verification (staging / self-signed only) |
| `--remote` | Use the named remote (URL + tls_verify from saved config); overrides the default remote for this command |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token (overrides global --token and saved config) |
| `--transport` | How to reach the vault: auto (default — a folder is local, an http(s) host is api unless its batch endpoint is absent), api (live SG/API), static (any GET host, read-only), local (a folder, read-only) One of: `api`, `auto`, `local`, `static`. |
| `--verify-tls` | Verify TLS certificates (default) |

---

*[Site index for agents](../llms.txt) · [HTML version](https://cli.sgit.ai/reference/clone-branch.html)*

# sgit clone, cli.sgit.ai

> Clone a vault from the remote server

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/reference/clone.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# sgit clone

Clone a vault from the remote server.

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.23.0. No subcommands. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit clone [options] <vault_key> [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `vault_key` | required | Vault key — one of: {passphrase}:{vault_id} (full clone), {read_key_hex}:{vault_id} (auto-detects read-only), or just {vault_id} when --read-key is set; - reads it from stdin (keeps it out of argv and history) |
| `directory` | optional | Directory to clone into (default: vault ID) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--bare` | Clone vault structure only — no working-copy files extracted (full implementation in B09; currently stubs) |
| `--base-url` | API base URL (overrides --remote, global --base-url, and saved config) |
| `--depth` | Shallow clone: fetch only the newest N commits of history (1 = HEAD only). Commit, push and pull work normally; history commands stop at the boundary (sgit fetch --unshallow). |
| `--force` | Delete existing directory and re-clone from scratch |
| `--no-verify-tls` | Skip TLS certificate verification (staging / self-signed only) |
| `--path` | Scoped clone: hold only this vault folder (repeatable). Other folders are carried by id and never downloaded; commits and pulls touch only the held folders. Widen later with sgit fetch <folder>. |
| `--read-key` | Read-only clone using a 64-hex AES-256 read key. When set, the positional vault_key is the vault_id only (no passphrase prefix). Equivalent shorthand: pass "<HEX>:<vault_id>" as the positional. |
| `--remote` | Use the named remote (URL + tls_verify from saved config); overrides the default remote for this command |
| `--sparse` | Download only structure (commits + trees); fetch file content on demand |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token (overrides global --token and saved config) |
| `--transport` | How to reach the vault: auto (default — a folder is local, an http(s) host is api unless its batch endpoint is absent), api (live SG/API), static (any GET host, read-only), local (a folder, read-only) One of: `api`, `auto`, `local`, `static`. |
| `--verify-tls` | Verify TLS certificates (default) |

---

*[Site index for agents](../llms.txt) · [HTML version](https://cli.sgit.ai/reference/clone.html)*

# sgit commit

Commit local changes to the clone branch.

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.23.0. No subcommands. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit commit [options] [message]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | optional | Commit message (auto-generated if omitted) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--allow-deletions` | In sparse clones, allow files absent from disk to be deleted (default: preserve unfetched entries) |
| `--allow-secret-file` | Commit PATH although it looks like a vault secret (a zip with a key file in it); names one file, repeatable |
| `--amend` | Replace the last commit (not yet pushed) with the working copy and/or a new -m message |
| `-d`, `--directory` | Vault directory (default: .) |
| `-m`, `--message` | Commit message via flag (git-style). Overrides the positional arg. |

# sgit create

Create a new vault and push it to the server in one step.

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.23.0. No subcommands. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit create [options] <vault_name>
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `vault_name` | required | Vault name / directory to create |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--base-url` | API base URL (overrides --remote, global --base-url, and saved config) |
| `--no-push` | Initialise locally but skip the initial push |
| `--no-verify-tls` | Skip TLS certificate verification (staging / self-signed only) |
| `--remote` | Use the named remote (URL + tls_verify from saved config); overrides the default remote for this command |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token (overrides global --token and saved config) |
| `--transport` | How to reach the vault: auto (default — a folder is local, an http(s) host is api unless its batch endpoint is absent), api (live SG/API), static (any GET host, read-only), local (a folder, read-only) One of: `api`, `auto`, `local`, `static`. |
| `--vault-key` | Vault key ({passphrase}:{vault_id}). Auto-generated if omitted. |
| `--verify-tls` | Verify TLS certificates (default) |

# sgit fetch, cli.sgit.ai

# sgit fetch

Fetch file content on demand (sparse clone).

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.23.0. No subcommands. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit fetch [options] [path] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | optional | File or directory path to fetch (default: all) |
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--all` | Fetch all unfetched files (convert sparse clone to full) |
| `--base-url` | API base URL (overrides --remote, global --base-url, and saved config) |
| `--no-verify-tls` | Skip TLS certificate verification (staging / self-signed only) |
| `--remote` | Use the named remote (URL + tls_verify from saved config); overrides the default remote for this command |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token (overrides global --token and saved config) |
| `--transport` | How to reach the vault: auto (default — a folder is local, an http(s) host is api unless its batch endpoint is absent), api (live SG/API), static (any GET host, read-only), local (a folder, read-only) One of: `api`, `auto`, `local`, `static`. |
| `--unshallow` | Shallow clone: fetch the history behind the boundary commit(s) |
| `--verify-tls` | Verify TLS certificates (default) |

---

# sgit file

File operations (cat, ls, write).

```text
sgit file
```

## Subcommands

- [`sgit file cat`](#file-cat): Decrypt and print a vault file to stdout
- [`sgit file ls`](#file-ls): List vault files with fetch status
- [`sgit file write`](#file-write): Write a file directly to vault HEAD (agent/programmatic workflow)

### sgit file cat {#file-cat}

Decrypt and print a vault file to stdout

```text
sgit file cat [options] <path> [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|

| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--id` | Print only the blob ID (zero network calls) |

### sgit file ls {#file-ls}

```text
sgit file ls [options] [path] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |

| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|

| `--json` | Output full entry metadata as JSON array |

```text
sgit file write [options] <path> [directory]
```

| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--also` | Additional files to include atomically (repeatable) |
| `--file` | Read content from LOCAL_FILE instead of stdin |
| `--json` | Print result as JSON instead of plain text |
| `--message` | Commit message (auto-generated if omitted) |
| `--push` | Push immediately after writing; stdout contains only the blob ID |

# sgit history, cli.sgit.ai

> Commit history and diffs

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/reference/history.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# sgit history

Commit history and diffs.

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.23.0. 7 subcommands below. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit history
```

## Subcommands

- [`sgit history diff`](#history-diff): Show file-level and content-level diff
- [`sgit history log`](#history-log): Show commit history
- [`sgit history reflog`](#history-reflog): Where this clone's head has pointed (local, newest first)
- [`sgit history reset`](#history-reset): Reset local branch HEAD to a specific commit (git reset --hard)
- [`sgit history revert`](#history-revert): Restore working copy files to a past commit
- [`sgit history show`](#history-show): Show changes introduced by a commit
- [`sgit history undo`](#history-undo): Move this clone's head back to where it was before its last move (local)

### sgit history diff {#history-diff}

Show file-level and content-level diff

```text
sgit history diff [options] [range_spec] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `range_spec` | optional | Commit range (e.g. abc..def); synonym for --commit A --commit2 B |
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--commit` | Compare working copy vs specific commit |
| `--commit2` | Second commit for commit-to-commit diff (requires --commit) |
| `--files-only` | Show file names only (no inline diff) |
| `--json` | Structured JSON output for agents |
| `--remote` | Compare working copy vs named branch HEAD |

### sgit history log {#history-log}

Show commit history

```text
sgit history log [options] [range_spec] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `range_spec` | optional | Commit range (e.g. abc..def); omit for full history |
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--author` | Only commits by WHO: a branch name exactly (alice matches alice, not alice-laptop: use --author alice-laptop), or a signing key id / branch id, whole or by 4+ hex at either end (--author 3f9a) |
| `--file` | Show only commits that touched this file |
| `--files` | Include files changed per commit (range mode) |
| `--graph` | Show graph with connectors |
| `--grep` | Only commits whose message matches (case-insensitive regular expression) |
| `--json` | Structured JSON output for agents (range mode) |
| `--oneline` | Compact one-line-per-commit format |
| `--patch` | Include full diff per commit (range mode) |
| `--since` | Only commits at or after WHEN (2026-10-08, 2026-10-08T14:30, 3d, 12h, "2 weeks ago") |
| `--stat` | List the files each commit added (A), modified (M), deleted (D) or renamed (R) |
| `--until` | Only commits before WHEN (same forms) |
| `--vault-key` | Vault key (auto-read from .sg_vault/local/vault_key if omitted) |
| `-n`, `--max-count` | Limit output to the last N commits |

### sgit history reflog {#history-reflog}

Where this clone's head has pointed (local, newest first)

```text
sgit history reflog [options] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--all` | Every local ref, not just this clone's head |
| `-n`, `--max-count` | Show the last N moves (default 20, 0 = all) |

### sgit history reset {#history-reset}

Reset local branch HEAD to a specific commit (git reset --hard)

```text
sgit history reset [commit_id] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `commit_id` | optional | Target commit ID (full or prefix); omit to discard working-copy changes |
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

### sgit history revert {#history-revert}

Restore working copy files to a past commit

```text
sgit history revert [options] [directory] [files]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |
| `files` | optional | Specific files to revert (default: all) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--as-commit` | Make a NEW commit that inverts --commit (git revert); push it to undo a pushed change for everyone |
| `--commit` | Revert to a specific commit (default: HEAD) |
| `--force` | Skip confirmation prompt when reverting all files |
| `-m`, `--message` | Message for --as-commit (default: Revert "<original>") |

### sgit history show {#history-show}

Show changes introduced by a commit

```text
sgit history show [options] <commit_id> [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `commit_id` | required | Commit ID to inspect |
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--files-only` | Show file names only (no inline diff) |

### sgit history undo {#history-undo}

Move this clone's head back to where it was before its last move (local)

```text
sgit history undo [options] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `directory` | optional | Vault directory (default: .) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--force` | Undo even when the head is already on the server (this clone only) |

---

# Command reference, cli.sgit.ai

> Every sgit command, subcommand, argument and option, generated from the CLI's own parser (sgit help all --format json), grouped by what it is for.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/reference/index.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# Command reference

All **158 commands** of **sgit-ai v0.23.0**, generated from the parser the CLI actually builds. The CLI walks its own argparse tree (`CLI__Reference`, behind `sgit help all --format json`, schema `sgit-cli-reference-v1`); this site renders that JSON and nothing else. A flag cannot appear here unless the code registers it, and none the code registers can be missing.

- The same data, as published: [sgit-cli-reference.json](../reference/sgit-cli-reference.json). Diff two releases' files to see exactly what changed.
- Your installed version, offline: `sgit help all`, or `sgit help <command>`.
- Global options go before the command: `sgit [--base-url URL] [--token TOKEN] [--vault PATH] [--debug] <command> ...`.

Where to put a new command is a rule of the CLI (its `CLAUDE.md`): a daily-use verb at the top level, anything about the vault as a whole under `vault`, anything about commits under `history`, checks under `check`.

### Daily work

| Command | Subcommands | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`sgit clone`](../reference/clone.md) |  | Clone a vault from the remote server |
| [`sgit init`](../reference/init.md) |  | Create a new empty vault and register it on the server |
| [`sgit create`](../reference/create.md) |  | Create a new vault and push it to the server in one step |
| [`sgit status`](../reference/status.md) |  | Show uncommitted changes in working directory |
| [`sgit commit`](../reference/commit.md) |  | Commit local changes to the clone branch |
| [`sgit pull`](../reference/pull.md) |  | Pull named branch changes and merge into clone branch |
| [`sgit push`](../reference/push.md) |  | Push clone branch to the named branch |
| [`sgit fetch`](../reference/fetch.md) |  | Fetch file content on demand (sparse clone) |
| [`sgit write`](../reference/write.md) |  | Write a file directly to vault HEAD (agent workflow) |
| [`sgit cat`](../reference/cat.md) |  | Decrypt and print a vault file to stdout |
| [`sgit ls`](../reference/ls.md) |  | List vault files with fetch status |
| [`sgit file`](../reference/file.md) | 3 | File operations (cat, ls, write) |
| [`sgit publish`](../reference/publish.md) |  | Generate the plaintext surface for static publishing (.sg_vault/publish/ — the only path that changes) |

### Branches and merges

| Command | Subcommands | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`sgit branch`](../reference/branch.md) | 7 | Branch management |
| [`sgit merge-abort`](../reference/merge-abort.md) |  | Abort an in-progress merge and restore working tree |
| [`sgit resolve`](../reference/resolve.md) |  | Resolve merge conflicts per file or all at once |

### History

| Command | Subcommands | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`sgit history`](../reference/history.md) | 7 | Commit history and diffs |

### The vault as a whole

| Command | Subcommands | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`sgit vault`](../reference/vault.md) | 41 | Vault management and credential store |
| [`sgit remote`](../reference/remote.md) | 7 | Manage vault remotes (alias for `sgit vault remote`) |
| [`sgit migrate`](../reference/migrate.md) | 3 | Run vault data migrations |
| [`sgit cache`](../reference/cache.md) | 4 | Declare cached paths (fast single-request reads) |

### Keys and identity

| Command | Subcommands | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`sgit pki`](../reference/pki.md) | 10 | PKI key management and encryption |

### Checking and looking inside

| Command | Subcommands | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`sgit check`](../reference/check.md) | 3 | Vault integrity checks |
| [`sgit inspect`](../reference/inspect.md) | 6 | Read-only vault inspection tools |
| [`sgit doctor`](../reference/doctor.md) |  | Check remote connectivity and configuration |

### Running a vault locally

| Command | Subcommands | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`sgit serve`](../reference/serve.md) | 8 | Run this vault on your machine: the vault UI + API in a container (Docker, Podman, Apple container), or --static |

### Other ways to clone

| Command | Subcommands | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`sgit clone-branch`](../reference/clone-branch.md) |  | Thin clone: full commit history + HEAD trees/blobs only. Note: only HEAD is fully fetched — run 'sgit fetch <path>' or 'sgit pull' to access older history. |
| [`sgit clone-headless`](../reference/clone-headless.md) |  | Credentials-only clone: derive keys, write config, no data |
| [`sgit clone-range`](../reference/clone-range.md) |  | Clone a specific commit range (range_from..range_to) |

### The tool itself

| Command | Subcommands | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`sgit help`](../reference/help.md) |  | Show help (use `sgit help all` for full surface) |
| [`sgit version`](../reference/version.md) |  | Show sgit-ai version |
| [`sgit update`](../reference/update.md) |  | Update sgit-ai to the latest version |

### For developers of sgit

| Command | Subcommands | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`sgit dev`](../reference/dev.md) | 26 | Dev/perf instrumentation tools (sgit dev <tool>) |

## How this page is made

`admin/content/reference/sgit-cli-reference.json` is the output of `sgit help all --format json` from the release named above, installed from PyPI. The build turns it into one page per top-level command. To update: install the new release, run the command into that file, rebuild, and say in the release history which version the reference moved to.

# sgit init, cli.sgit.ai

> Create a new empty vault and register it on the server

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/reference/init.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# sgit init

Create a new empty vault and register it on the server.

*Generated from `sgit help all --format json`, sgit-ai v0.23.0. No subcommands. To change this page, change the command's `register()` in the CLI and regenerate.*

```text
sgit init [options] [directory]
```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `directory` | optional | Directory to create the vault in (default: current directory) |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--base-url` | API base URL (overrides --remote, global --base-url, and saved config) |
| `--existing` | Allow initialising into a non-empty directory without prompting |
| `--no-verify-tls` | Skip TLS certificate verification (staging / self-signed only) |
| `--remote` | Use the named remote (URL + tls_verify from saved config); overrides the default remote for this command |
| `--restore` | Restore vault from a .vault__*.zip backup in the target directory |
| `--token` | SG/Send access token (overrides global --token and saved config) |
| `--transport` | How to reach the vault: auto (default — a folder is local, an http(s) host is api unless its batch endpoint is absent), api (live SG/API), static (any GET host, read-only), local (a folder, read-only) One of: `api`, `auto`, `local`, `static`. |
| `--vault-key` | Vault key ({passphrase}:{vault_id}). Generated randomly if omitted. |
| `--verify-tls` | Verify TLS certificates (default) |

---

|---|---|---|

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|

```text

```

| Argument | | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `file` | required | File to encrypt |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--fingerprint` | Your key fingerprint (for signing) |
| `--output`, `-o` | Output file (default: FILE.enc) |
| `--recipient` | Recipient fingerprint (a contact or one of your key pairs) |

### sgit pki export {#pki-export}

Export public key bundle (JSON)

| Argument | | What it is |


| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--label` | Label for the key pair |


|---|---|---|
| `file` | required | File to verify |
| `signature` | required | Signature file (.sig) |

| Option | What it does |
