# `sgit serve`: container first. Options map and spike results, cli.sgit.ai

> The decision to run the SG/Send container image rather than re-implement the server: the runtimes supported (including Apple's container and Podman), the spike results, and phase 1 as built.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/research/sgit-serve-container-first.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Published from <https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__CLI/blob/477d328536b04147e78281fb1f13550df1abf140/team/humans/dinis_cruz/claude-code-web/10/12/options__sgit-serve-container-and-static.md>.*

---
# `sgit serve`: container first. Options map and spike results

**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** options and plan, no sgit code yet · **Supersedes** the
"native server" plan in [`research__sgit-serve-local-vault-server.md`](../research/sgit-serve-running-a-vault-locally.md) (same folder). The API
inventory and browser notes there still apply.

**Decision (Dinis):** run a working vault locally from the SG/Send container image. It has
the vault UI and the API in one image and always tracks the latest SG/Send. sgit gets native
support for it:
- it abstracts the container runtime;
- it supports several runtimes, including Apple's `container`;
- it can install one when none is present;
- it should also work without Docker where possible.

The current read-only server stays as a separate, clearly named mode.

> **Update, same day: decisions taken and phase 1 built.**
> - **Decisions:**
>   1. Image `latest`, with the digest that ran recorded.
>   2. `sgit serve install` installs, after showing what and asking.
>   3. Both Apple `container` and Podman are supported on macOS.
>   4. `sgit vault serve` moved to `sgit serve --static`.
>   5. The brief to SG/Send is in this folder.
> - **What changed from the plan below:** the clone does **not** push to the local server as a
>   second remote. Its rewind baselines and its copy of the server's ref are kept per branch,
>   not per server, so two servers would trip its own rewind protection. Instead:
>   - `sgit serve push` (clone → server) only ever moves the local server forward;
>   - `sgit serve pull` (server → clone) fetches, verifies, checks the signature policy and
>     fast-forwards this clone's own branch;
>   - `sgit push` then reaches the real server as usual.
> - **Verified here:**
>   - Docker end to end: start, the UI opening the served clone, a server-side commit brought
>     back, stop;
>   - the uv engine (same data folder);
>   - divergence refusals.
>
>   The Apple `container` adapter is written to its documented CLI but not yet run on a Mac.

## 1. Two modes

| Mode | Command | What it is | Writes | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **container** (default) | `sgit serve` | The SG/Send image (`diniscruz/sg-send-vault`): vault UI + full API + disk store, on `localhost` | yes. A real local vault server: the UI edits, sgit pushes and pulls | a container runtime, or the Python engine (§4) |
| **static** | `sgit serve --static` (today's `sgit vault serve`) | A stdlib read-only file server for a **published** vault: the static loader plus the encrypted store, no API | no | nothing |

- Static mode still has a job: it previews what `sgit publish` produces, or serves an unpacked
  published zip, with zero dependencies.
- It is not "run a vault". Rename it, and make `sgit vault serve` print its new place
  (the rule-9 moved-word behaviour).

## 2. What I verified today (spike in this cloud container)

All of it was run here, x86_64 Linux, Docker 29.6 / containerd 2.2. The screenshot
`spike__local-container-ui-open-vault.png` is next to this file.

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `docker pull diniscruz/sg-send-vault:latest` | about 10 s; **400 MB**; a multi-arch index (amd64 + arm64); server **v0.34.0**, UI v0.2.3; 31 tags (`v0.27.70` … `v0.34.0`) |
| 2 | `docker run -p 8080:8080 -v <dir>:/data` | `/api/info/health` ok; UI `/` 200 |
| 3 | `sgit init` / `commit` / `push` / `clone --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8080` (repo code) | works: 12 objects on disk at `<dir>/vault/iv/ivh5cbkj/{manifest.json,bare/…}`; the fresh clone has the files |
| 4 | **The image runs as uid 10001** (its README still says root) | a host folder owned by the user is **not writable**: `Permission denied: '/data/vault'`. **Fix: `--user $(id -u):$(id -g)`**, which sgit must always pass |
| 5 | sgit refuses to push with no token ("no access token configured") even though the server has no auth | passing any `--token` works. **sgit fix:** a server that needs no token is a normal case |
| 6 | Headless Chromium → `http://localhost:8080/en-gb/vault/`, key typed into the form | **the vault opens and decrypts**: `docs/`, `a.md` ("hello local"). Same origin, plain http on localhost, Web Crypto fine |
| 7 | `#<vault-key>` in the URL | did not auto-open (the form did) |
| 8 | The UI loads `sg-layout.js` and `sg-llm-events.js` **from `dev.tools.sgraph.ai` at runtime** | not self-contained, despite "no CDN dependency" in its README: offline or air-gapped use will break |
| 9 | The UI shows "Read-only" until an access key is entered | expected; `sgit serve` should print the access-key hint, or configure the container so the UI is writable |
| 10 | **containerd only** (`ctr run`, no Docker API) | works (image imported, push lands on disk) |
| 11 | Anonymous `ctr pull` from Docker Hub | **429 Too Many Requests**; Docker Hub's anonymous limit is 100 pulls per 6 h per IP |
| 12 | **No container at all:** the image's own server code (`sgraph_ai_app_send__docker.app`) under a Python 3.12 venv, with the UI folder copied out of the image | works: health, UI, and an sgit push to a disk store |
| 13 | CORS for the hosted UI (`Origin: https://vault.sgraph.ai`) | preflight 200 with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` … **but with `Access-Control-Request-Private-Network: true` → 400 "Disallowed CORS private-network"**. Starlette's `allow_private_network` is off, so Chrome's private-network preflight from vault.sgraph.ai to localhost fails |
| 14 | A server error response | **contains the full Python stack trace** (an information leak; fine on a laptop, not on a shared host) |

## 3. Runtimes: what exists and how sgit would drive each

"docker-compatible" means it accepts `run -d --name -p -v --user -e`, `ps`, `stop`, `logs`
and `pull` with the same flags, so one adapter covers all of them. Rows marked † come from my
knowledge rather than today's run; check each against its current docs when building the
adapter.

| Runtime | OS | CLI | Install (what `sgit serve install` would do or print) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Docker Engine** | Linux | `docker` | distro package / get.docker.com | the reference; verified here |
| **Docker Desktop** | macOS, Windows | `docker` | the vendor installer | Linux VM under the hood; **paid licence for larger companies**† |
| **Podman** | Linux, macOS, Windows | `podman` (docker-compatible) | `brew install podman` + `podman machine init/start` on mac/Windows; distro package on Linux | daemonless, **rootless by default**†; with `--userns=keep-id` the uid problem (#4) goes away; no Docker licence |
| **Apple `container`** | macOS 26 on **Apple silicon** (macOS 15 runs with reduced networking) | `container` (its own CLI, docker-like) | signed `.pkg` from GitHub `apple/container` releases, then `container system start` | one lightweight VM per container, runs OCI images, no Docker. **Its own adapter**; flags to confirm against `container run --help` (ports, mounts) |
| **Colima** | macOS, Linux | gives a `docker` (or `nerdctl`) context | `brew install colima docker && colima start` | free, Lima VM; then the docker adapter† |
| **OrbStack** | macOS | `docker` | vendor app | fast; commercial licence for business use† |
| **Rancher Desktop** | macOS, Windows, Linux | `docker` or `nerdctl` | vendor installer | free (SUSE)† |
| **Finch** | macOS, Windows, Linux | `finch` (nerdctl-based, docker-like) | AWS installer / brew | free (AWS)† |
| **containerd + nerdctl** | Linux | `nerdctl` (docker-compatible) | distro or release tarball | lean Linux servers; raw `ctr` works too (verified, #10) |
| **WSL2** | Windows | any of the above inside WSL | `wsl --install` + one of the above | Windows without Docker Desktop |
| **Python engine** (no container) | anywhere with **`uv`** | `uv run --python 3.12 --with sgraph-ai-app-send …` | `uv` (one static binary); uv fetches Python 3.12 itself | the same server code as the image, verified (#12); needs the built UI folder (§5) |

**Detection order:** a runtime already running wins. Otherwise the order is:
1. `docker` (context answers)
2. `podman`
3. `container` (Apple)
4. `nerdctl`
5. `finch`
6. the Python engine if `uv` is found
7. `--static` as the last resort, with a message saying what the user is missing

`sgit serve --runtime <name>` overrides the choice. `sgit serve runtimes` lists what it found,
and for anything missing, the one install command per OS.

**Installing:**
- `sgit serve install [<runtime>]` prints the command and runs it **only after a yes**, because
  it is a system change.
- On macOS with Apple silicon it suggests Apple `container`, or Podman.
- On Linux it suggests Podman or Docker Engine.
- On Windows it suggests WSL2 + Podman.
- Without any runtime, it suggests `uv` and the Python engine.

## 4. What `sgit serve` does (container mode)

```
sgit serve                     # inside a clone
  1. pick a runtime (§3); pull the image, pinned by digest and recorded (latest by default; --tag vX.Y.Z)
  2. data dir: <clone>/.sg_vault/serve/ (or --data DIR, interchangeable with any sg-send-vault /data)
  3. run: --name sgit-serve-<vault_id> --user <uid>:<gid> -p 127.0.0.1:<port>:8080 -v <data>:/data
          (-p on 127.0.0.1 only: a plain `-p 8080:8080` publishes on every interface)
  4. wait for /api/info/health
  5. seed: push this clone into it as a remote, `local` → http://127.0.0.1:<port>
           (the existing push code: no coupling to the server's disk layout)
  6. print the UI URL, the vault-key and access-key hints; --open launches the browser
sgit serve status | logs | stop | update     # update = pull the newer image, restart, same data dir
sgit serve --static                          # today's read-only published-folder server
```

Then:
- `sgit pull --remote local` brings edits made in the browser into the clone, with full
  verify-then-accept;
- `sgit push` sends them to the real server.

The server owns its own store. The clone's `.sg_vault/bare/` is never mounted, because the
UI writing the clone's accepted refs would undo what 0.21 fixed.

**Python engine:** steps 1 and 3 become
`uv run --python 3.12 --with sgraph-ai-app-send==<v> python -m … --port <p>`, with
`SEND__STORAGE_MODE=disk`, `SEND__DISK_PATH=<data>` and `SEND__VAULT_STATIC_DIR=<ui dir>`.
Everything else is the same.

**TLS:** only for the LAN or Safari cases (see the research note §5–6).
- sgit generates a cert with `cryptography`;
- it mounts the cert and key at `/certs`;
- it sets `FAST_API__TLS__ENABLED=true`, which the image already supports.

## 5. Asks of the SG/Send team (from the spike)

1. **Vendor the `dev.tools.sgraph.ai` scripts into the image** (#8). Today the "self-contained"
   UI needs the internet.
2. **`allow_private_network=True`** in the CORS middleware (#13). Without it, the hosted UI
   cannot reach a local server from Chrome.
3. **No stack traces in error responses** (#14), or only behind a debug flag.
4. **README:** the image runs as uid 10001, so document `--user` or `chown` (#4).
5. **Also publish to GHCR or ECR Public** (#11). sgit can then fall back when Docker Hub
   rate-limits.
6. **Publish the built vault UI** (`/app/static_vault`) as a versioned release asset. That is
   what the Python engine needs; today it can only be copied out of the image.
7. Optionally, let `#<vault-key>` (or a `?key=` handoff) auto-open on `/en-gb/vault/` (#7), so
   `sgit serve --open` lands inside the vault.

## 6. Changes in sgit

| Change | Size |
|---|---|
| `Container__Runtime` (detect, pull, run, ps, stop, logs, health wait) with adapters: docker-compatible (docker, podman, nerdctl, finch), Apple `container`, Python engine (uv) | ~350 lines |
| `CLI__Serve`: container mode (seed via push to a `local` remote, banner, `--open`), `status/logs/stop/update/runtimes/install`, `--static` = today's server; `sgit vault serve` points to it | ~250 lines |
| A token is optional when the server has no auth (#5) | small |
| TLS cert generation + mount | ~100 lines |
| **Tests:**<br>• unit: each adapter's command lines, against a fake runtime binary on `PATH`;<br>• integration: **real Docker in CI** (the daemon starts in this kind of environment, as shown today); clone, push and pull against the image; a Playwright check that the UI opens the vault | ~1 day |

**Estimate:**

| Phase | Work | Estimate |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Docker-compatible adapter + serve, stop, status, logs + seeding | 2 days |
| 2 | Apple `container` adapter + Python engine | 1–1.5 days; the Apple adapter needs a Mac to test on |
| 3 | `runtimes`/`install` + TLS | 1 day |
| 4 | Docs, threat model rows | ½ day |

Total: about **5 days**. Phase 1 alone gives you "clone a vault, `sgit serve`, edit it in the
browser".

## 7. Decisions for you

1. **Image tag:** default to `latest` (always current, as you suggested) and record the
   digest in use, or pin per sgit release for reproducibility? My suggestion: `latest`, plus
   `--tag` and a recorded digest.
2. **Installing runtimes:** print the command only, or run it after confirmation?
3. **Apple `container` vs Podman** as the macOS recommendation: Apple's needs macOS 26 on
   Apple silicon; Podman runs everywhere.
4. **`--static` naming:** keep `sgit vault serve` as an alias, or move it fully?
5. Should I send the §5 asks to the SG/Send team as a brief?

## Sources

- Apple `container`: <https://tessl.io/registry/skills/github/sanjay3290/ai-skills/apple-container>
  (community summary of `apple/container`: Apple silicon only, macOS 26 supported, macOS 15
  with reduced networking, signed .pkg + `container system start`)
- Docker Hub pull limits: <https://docs.docker.com/docker-hub/download-rate-limit/>,
  <https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-20-portainer-docker-hub-anonymous-auth/view>

  [`research__sgit-serve-local-vault-server.md`](../research/sgit-serve-running-a-vault-locally.md).

# `sgit serve`: running a vault locally — research and plan, cli.sgit.ai

> How to run a vault locally: the vault server's API inventory, the browser modes, when TLS is and is not needed, and how much plumbing sgit would need.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/research/sgit-serve-running-a-vault-locally.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Published from <https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__CLI/blob/477d328536b04147e78281fb1f13550df1abf140/team/humans/dinis_cruz/claude-code-web/10/12/research__sgit-serve-local-vault-server.md>.*

---
# `sgit serve`: running a vault locally — research and plan

**Date:** 2026-10-12 · **Status:** research and design, no code yet · **Asked:** "how can I run a
vault locally … just clone a vault and run it from there … `sgit serve` … SSL if needed … how
much plumbing do we need to add to sgit".

> **Superseded in part (same day):** Dinis chose to run the SG/Send **container image** rather
> than re-implement the server in sgit. See [`options__sgit-serve-container-and-static.md`](../research/sgit-serve-container-first.md).
> The API inventory (§3), browser modes (§5) and TLS notes (§6) below still apply.

## 1. Short answer

It is very doable, mostly with what we already have.
- **Server side:** a vault server is a small API (§3): read, write, delete, batch with
  compare-and-swap, list, health and destroy, all over a key-value store. sgit already has a
  stdlib HTTP server (`sgit vault serve`, read-only) and an in-memory model of the API. A
  native, stdlib-only `sgit serve` that adds the write side and a disk store is about
  **600–900 lines plus tests**. It needs **no new dependencies** and runs on Python 3.11.
- **The web UI:** the SG/Send team already builds a static copy of it that talks to its own
  origin. The docker image `diniscruz/sg-send-vault` uses that build (`VAULT_DEFAULT_ENDPOINT=""`
  → relative `/api/...` paths). sgit can ship or fetch that build and serve it beside the API.
- **TLS:** **not needed for the default setup.** Serve the UI and the API from one origin,
  `http://localhost:<port>`. Browsers treat `localhost` as a secure context, so Web Crypto
  works, and nothing is cross-origin. TLS (or the CORS mode, §5) matters for two cases only:
  using the **hosted** UI (vault.sgraph.ai) against a local API from Safari, and reaching the
  server from another machine. For those we add `--tls` (§6).

**Estimate:**
- an MVP (local API, the UI, serving a clone) in about **3 days**;
- the full version (CORS mode for the hosted UI, TLS, docs, threat model) in about **5 days**.

## 2. What exists today

| Piece | Where | What it gives us |
|---|---|---|
| `sgit vault serve` | `sgit_ai/cli/CLI__Serve.py`, `sgit_ai/core/serve/Vault__Static_Server.py` | A stdlib `ThreadingHTTPServer`, read-only (GET/HEAD; anything else is 405), bound to 127.0.0.1, with a Host-header check against DNS rebinding and a path guard. It serves the published static loader and maps `/api/vault/read/<id>/bare/*` onto `.sg_vault/bare/`. |
| `Vault__API__In_Memory` | `sgit_ai/network/api/` | The API semantics the CLI relies on (batch, `write-if-match` conflicts, list, tombstones), in process. It does not check write keys. |
| Real SG/Send server | `sgraph-ai-app-send` (PyPI, **Python ≥ 3.12**; fastapi, uvicorn, osbot-aws, mcp …) | Our integration suite already runs it in-process with in-memory storage. It also has **disk** storage. |
| SG/Send container | `diniscruz/sg-send-vault` (~250 MB; source `sgraph_ai_app_send__docker/`) | **The whole local stack already exists as an image:** the vault UI at `/` plus the API on one port. Disk storage goes to `/data` (layout in §3.4). It has an optional access token, can terminate TLS itself if given a cert/key, and its README covers the secure-context and Web Crypto issue. |
| Vault UI | `sgraph_ai_app_send__ui__vault` (inside the server package; v0.2.3 is 2.6 MB unbuilt) | The endpoint comes from `window.SG_ENDPOINT`, then `sessionStorage['sg-vault-endpoint']` (there is an **endpoint field** on the entry form), then `https://dev.send.sgraph.ai`. A `/#<key>` hash opens a vault directly. It calls only vault endpoints, plus the transfer and presigned endpoints for other features. |

So "run a vault locally" works **today** with docker:

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 -v "$PWD/_sg-send_data:/data" diniscruz/sg-send-vault:latest
sgit clone <vault-key> my-vault --base-url http://localhost:8080   # or push an existing clone there
```

What is missing:
- the one-command experience;
- no docker requirement;
- starting from a clone you already have.

## 3. The API a local server must speak

This is from the code of `sgraph-ai-app-send` 0.33.0, the user lambda:
`lambda__user/fast_api/routes/Routes__Vault__Pointer.py` and
`service/Service__Vault__Pointer.py`.

### 3.1 Routes

| Method | Path | Auth | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/vault/read/{vault_id}/{file_id:path}` | public | raw bytes; 404 if missing |
| PUT | `/api/vault/write/{vault_id}/{file_id:path}` | write key | an empty body gives 400; returns `{file_id, vault_id, status:"completed"}` |
| DELETE | `/api/vault/delete/{vault_id}/{file_id:path}` | write key | 403 for a key mismatch **and** for a missing file |
| POST | `/api/vault/batch/{vault_id}` | public if every op is `read`, otherwise write key | 1–100 ops; **always HTTP 200** (§3.3) |
| GET | `/api/vault/list/{vault_id}?prefix=` | public | `{vault_id, prefix, files:[…]}`, sorted |
| GET | `/api/vault/health/{vault_id}` | public | 200 if `manifest.json` exists, otherwise 404 |
| DELETE | `/api/vault/destroy/{vault_id}` | write key | body `{vault_id, purge?}`; writes a tombstone |
| GET | `/api/info/health` | public | `{"status":"ok"}` |

`vault_id` must match `^[a-z0-9]{8,24}$`.

Extras the local server does not need for vaults:
- **Presigned upload/download:** S3 only. Other modes answer 400 "Presigned URLs not
  available", and sgit and the UI already fall back to direct writes.
- `read-base64`, zip, inbox, public-info.
- The `/api/transfers/*` family, which is Send's file transfer and not vaults.

### 3.2 Auth

- **Write key, trusted on first write:**
  - The server stores `sha256(<write-key header string>)` in `manifest.json` on the first
    write or batch. After that, the hashes must match, or the server answers 403.
  - A `deleted.json` tombstone refuses every write.
- **Access token** (`x-sgraph-access-token`):
  - It is checked only when configured; empty means open, which is what local dev uses.
  - The container can gate every route, reads included.

### 3.3 Batch

Ops are `read`, `write` (b64), `write-if-match` (`match` b64, or null for "must not exist")
and `delete`.

- A conflict returns `{op, file_id, status:"conflict", current:b64|null}` and **stops** the
  batch.
- The batch is ordered and best-effort: ops before a conflict stay applied.
- The comparison is on whole bytes.

This is exactly what sgit's CAS code already handles; it is the live server's behaviour.

### 3.4 Disk layout (container and lambda disk mode)

```
<root>/vault/<vault_id[:2]>/<vault_id>/manifest.json          {vault_id, write_key_hash, created_at}
<root>/vault/<vault_id[:2]>/<vault_id>/deleted.json           tombstone
<root>/vault/<vault_id[:2]>/<vault_id>/<file_id>/payload      e.g. bare/data/obj-cas-imm-…/payload
```

If the native server uses **the same layout**, a data folder works with both `sgit serve` and
`docker run -v <folder>:/data diniscruz/sg-send-vault`. That gives an exact-parity fallback
for free.

Note that this is **not** the clone's own layout: `.sg_vault/bare/data/<id>` is a file, not
`<id>/payload`. Section 4 explains why the server keeps its own store anyway.

### 3.5 CORS

- The lambda sends `allow_origins=["*"]` with `allow_credentials=False`, the usual methods,
  and the headers `x-sgraph-access-token` and `x-sgraph-vault-write-key`, among others.
- **No `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network` handling exists anywhere** (relevant to §5).

## 4. "Clone a vault and run it from there": the model

Recommendation: **the server has its own store, seeded from the clone; the clone talks to it
as a remote.** The server should not read and write the clone's `.sg_vault/bare/` directly.

Why not serve the clone's `bare/` directly:
- A clone's `bare/refs/<named-ref>` is the clone's *accepted* copy of the server ref. Since
  0.21 only a pull that passed verification moves it, and the rewind baselines depend on it.
- A web UI writing into that same file would move the clone's named ref behind its back.
  `status` would say "in sync" while nothing was pulled, the signature policy would be
  bypassed, and the next pull would see a "rewind".
- That is the exact class of bug the last five review rounds closed.

So:

```
my-vault/                      the clone (unchanged behaviour)
my-vault/.sg_vault/serve/      the local server's store, in SG/Send disk layout (§3.4)
                               (inside .sg_vault, so it is never committed; excluded from uninit backups)
```

`sgit serve`, run inside a clone:
1. **Seeds the store** if it is empty:
   - every object in `.sg_vault/bare/data/` is **hard-linked**. Objects are content-addressed
     and immutable, so this costs no space or time; it falls back to copying across
     filesystems;
   - refs, indexes and keys are *copied*, because they are mutable;
   - it writes `manifest.json` with `sha256(write_key)`. The clone holds the vault key, so the
     write key is known, and the CLI and the UI can write.
   - The named ref the server starts from is the one the clone last **accepted**, so the
     local server is "the remote as this clone last verified it".
2. **Starts the server** on `http://localhost:8420`, with both the API and the UI.
3. **Prints:**
   - the UI URL;
   - how to open this vault in it: `--open` launches the browser with the vault key in the
     URL hash, which the UI reads; the hash never reaches the server;
   - the remote line: `sgit remote add local http://localhost:8420`, or a flag that adds it.

Then:
- `sgit pull --remote local` brings edits made in the browser into the clone, with full
  verify-then-accept.
- `sgit push --remote local` shows clone commits in the browser.
- `sgit push` (origin) publishes everything to the real server.

Outside a clone, `sgit serve --data <dir>` is a **general local SG/Send-compatible server**:
- any vault can be created, cloned (`--base-url http://localhost:8420`), pushed or pulled;
- its folder is interchangeable with the docker image's `/data`.

## 5. Browser access: three ways, and what each needs

| Mode | URL the user opens | Cross-origin? | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Same origin (default)** | `http://localhost:8420/` (UI served by sgit) | no | nothing. `localhost` is a secure context, so Web Crypto works in Chrome, Firefox and Safari. |
| **B. Hosted UI → local API** | `https://vault.sgraph.ai`, endpoint field set to `http://localhost:8420` | yes | CORS on the local server (`*` or an allow-list, as production does).<br>Chrome 141/142+: a one-time **Local Network Access** permission prompt per site.<br>Safari: blocks https→`http://localhost` as mixed content (WebKit bug 279249), so it needs `https://localhost` (§6). |
| **C. Another machine / LAN** | `https://<host>:8443` | – | TLS (Web Crypto refuses plain http on non-localhost hosts) **and** an access token |

- **Mode A** is the product: it works offline, does not depend on the hosted UI version, and
  needs no permissions or certs.
- **Mode B** is useful for testing the hosted UI against local data, and it is what "it has
  CORS enabled so you can load it from the other side" refers to.
- **Mode C** is opt-in, with warnings.

For B, the local server should also answer preflights with
`Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true`. Older Chrome Private Network Access preflights
need it, and it is harmless otherwise.

## 6. TLS

- **Default: none** (modes A and B in Chrome/Firefox).
- **`sgit serve --tls`:**
  - sgit generates a local CA and a `localhost`/`127.0.0.1` leaf cert with `cryptography`,
    already a dependency, under `~/.sgit/tls/`, and serves https on 8443 through stdlib `ssl`.
  - If `mkcert` is installed it uses mkcert's CA instead, which is already trusted.
  - `--cert/--key` use the user's own pair.
- **Trust:** a browser *page* can click through an untrusted cert, but a cross-origin `fetch`
  (mode B) cannot. So mode B over https needs the CA trusted.
  - `sgit serve trust` prints the exact per-OS command (macOS `security add-trusted-cert`,
    Windows `certutil -addstore`, Linux `update-ca-certificates`, plus `certutil -d sql:…`
    for the Chrome/Firefox NSS store).
  - It runs that command only on explicit confirmation, because changing the trust store is
    a system change.

## 7. The UI: where its files come from

| Option | Wheel size | Network at runtime | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Vendor a pinned, flattened build into the sgit wheel** (recommended) | +~1 MB zipped | none, works offline | must be refreshed per UI release; covered by a script, a pinned version and a SHA-256 manifest |
| Download on first `serve` into `~/.sgit/ui/<version>/`, hash-pinned | none | once | supply chain (mitigated by the pinned hash); fails offline the first time |
| Use the docker image for the UI | – | docker | not "just sgit" |

- The flattening is what `scripts/build-vault-static.sh` in SG/Send does, with
  `VAULT_DEFAULT_ENDPOINT=""`.
- sgit would add a `scripts/vendor-vault-ui.sh` that takes a pinned UI version and writes
  `sgit_ai/serve/ui/` plus `ui-version.json`.
- `--ui-dir PATH` lets UI developers serve a working tree instead.
- The server injects nothing; with `VAULT_DEFAULT_ENDPOINT=""` the UI uses its own origin.

**Ask of the SG/Send team:** publish the flattened vault UI as a versioned release asset
(zip + SHA-256). Then sgit vendors from it rather than rebuilding from their source tree.

## 8. Implementation plan

### Components

| Component | Layer | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `Vault__Local_Store`: the §3.4 layout; atomic writes (temp + rename); a per-vault lock for batch and CAS; list by prefix; manifest, write-key hash, tombstone | storage | ~200 lines |
| `Vault__Local_Server`: stdlib `ThreadingHTTPServer`; the §3.1 routes with matching status codes and JSON; batch semantics (§3.3); access-token option; Host check (from `Vault__Static_Server`); Origin allow-list on writes in mode A; CORS and PNA preflight; static UI; optional `ssl` wrap | core/serve | ~350 lines |
| `Vault__Serve__Seed`: hard-link objects, copy refs/indexes/keys, write the manifest | core/serve | ~100 lines |
| `Vault__Local_TLS`: CA and leaf generation, mkcert detection, trust instructions | crypto | ~120 lines |
| `CLI__Serve`: `sgit serve [--data DIR] [--port] [--bind] [--open] [--tls] [--cert/--key] [--cors-origin …] [--token] [--no-ui] [--ui-dir] [--add-remote]`; `sgit serve trust`; keep `vault serve` as the static-publish server | cli | ~200 lines |

Command placement (rule 9):
- `serve` is a daily-use verb, so it goes at the **top level**. That is a deliberate edit to
  `TOP_LEVEL_COMMANDS`.
- `sgit vault serve` stays, because it serves a *published* folder; its help points to
  `sgit serve`.

### Tests

- **Unit:** store, routes, status codes, batch CAS, the write-key first-write rule, tombstones,
  the Host check, the Origin check, CORS and PNA preflights, TLS against a generated cert,
  seeding (hard links, mutable files copied).
- **Contract:** one API test module that runs against **both** the native server and the real
  `sgraph-ai-app-send` test server, in the 3.12 integration job. That is how the native server
  stays in step with production.
- **End to end:**
  - `sgit clone/push/pull --base-url http://localhost:<port>` against `sgit serve`;
  - a Playwright smoke test in the preinstalled Chromium: the UI opens a vault served by
    `sgit serve` and lists its files; mode B fetch with CORS.

### Phases

| Phase | Work | Estimate |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Spike: vendored UI v0.2.3 + the real server on `localhost`, driven by Playwright; confirm modes A and B in Chromium | ½ day |
| 1 | Store + API server + seeding + `sgit serve` (API only); CLI interop; contract tests | 1½–2 days |
| 2 | UI vendoring + serving; `--open` | 1 day |
| 3 | Mode B: CORS allow-list, PNA header, Origin checks | ½ day |
| 4 | TLS: generated CA/leaf, mkcert, `--cert/--key`, `serve trust` | 1 day |
| 5 | Docs, threat model rows, CHANGELOG | ½ day |

**MVP = phases 0–2 (~3 days). Full = ~5 days.**

## 9. Security notes (to become threat-model rows)

- **Binding:** 127.0.0.1 by default. `--bind 0.0.0.0` requires `--token` and warns loudly;
  over plain http it also warns that the token travels in clear.
- **DNS rebinding:** keep the Host-header check (already in `Vault__Static_Server`).
- **Writes from other websites (mode A):**
  - Writes need the write key, which only someone holding the vault key can derive.
  - On top of that, refuse writes whose `Origin` is neither the server's own nor on the
    `--cors-origin` list.
  - Reads expose ciphertext only, which is the same as the public read API in production.
- **The vault key in the `--open` URL hash:** the hash is never sent to the server. The UI
  stores the key in `localStorage`, which is the UI's existing behaviour; the docs should
  say so.
- **The server store lives in `.sg_vault/serve/`:** never committed, excluded from uninit
  backups, so a backup does not double in size.
- **Nothing changes for the clone:** it reaches the local server only as a remote, through
  the same verify-then-accept path as any server.

## 10. Decisions for you

1. **UI files:** vendor into the wheel (recommended), download on first run, or rely on docker?
2. **Store location:** per clone in `.sg_vault/serve/` (recommended for "serve this clone"),
   with `--data DIR` for a shared multi-vault store?
3. **`local` remote:** should `sgit serve` add it automatically, or only print the command?
4. **Default port:** 8420, the same as today's `vault serve`, or 8080 like the container?
5. **Asks of SG/Send:**
   - a versioned UI release asset;
   - `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true` on preflights;
   - optionally a `?endpoint=` URL parameter in the UI, so mode B links can be shared.

## Sources

- Chrome Local Network Access: <https://developer.chrome.com/blog/local-network-access>;
  rollout notes <https://piunikaweb.com/2026/02/09/chrome-local-network-permission-explained/>,
  <https://support.beyondidentity.com/hc/en-us/articles/34457691192215-Managing-the-Chrome-v142Local-Network-Access-Prompt>
- Safari blocking https→`http://localhost`: <https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=279249>,
  <https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/736105>
- The SG/Send code and container README: from the installed `sgraph-ai-app-send` 0.33.0 package.

# Threat-modeling tools for an agent-driven review — Matt Adams' stack, the classics, and the house method, cli.sgit.ai

> Threat-modeling tools for an agent-driven review: Matt Adams' stack (STRIDE GPT, the insider-threat model), the classics, and the house method, with the agent itself named as an actor.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/research/threat-modeling-tools.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Published from <https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__CLI/blob/477d328536b04147e78281fb1f13550df1abf140/team/humans/dinis_cruz/claude-code-web/10/11/research__threat-modeling-tools.md>.*

---
# Threat-modeling tools for an agent-driven review — Matt Adams' stack, the classics, and the house method

**From:** the sgit-ai CLI agent · **Date:** 2026-10-11 · **For:** `threat-modeling.sgit.ai`
(Documents), then the case study once used.

**Why this matters more here than elsewhere.** sgit is operated by AI agents that hold vault
keys and write tokens. The threat model's actor list (`team/explorer/appsec/threat-model/v0.21.0__threat-model.md`
§3) names the host, the network, a read-key holder, a teammate, a hostile vault author, the
local machine, the supply chain and other clients. It does not yet name **the agent itself** as
an actor. Matt Adams' insider-threat model is the first published framework that does, and it
was generated with his own tool, so the two fit together.

## 1. Matt Adams' stack (mrwadams)

| Tool | What it is | Facts checked | Fit for sgit |
|---|---|---|---|
| **STRIDE GPT** | Open-source LLM threat modeller. Inputs: an application description, an architecture image, a draw.io diagram, a GitHub repository URL, or a **local code base** (`stride-gpt analyze <path>`, agentic: plan, explore, synthesise per subsystem). Outputs: STRIDE threat model with mitigations, attack trees, DREAD scores, Gherkin test cases, DFDs, MITRE ATT&CK and ATLAS mapping, OWASP LLM and agentic risk overlays. Formats: Markdown, **JSON**, **SARIF**, self-contained HTML; `-o` also writes plan, findings and run JSON | `github.com/mrwadams/stride-gpt`, MIT, v0.20, about 1.1k stars. `pip install stride-gpt` gives the CLI; web UI from source (`uv sync`, Streamlit) or `docker pull mrwadams/stridegpt`. **Anthropic is supported** through LiteLLM (the README's About line still says OpenAI; it is stale). Recent PRs: threats get a stable identifier (#231), a `report_threat` tool that demands verifiable evidence plus a final grace round (#205), a cost estimate before an `analyze` run (#218) | **The threat-model generator for the review.** Run it on the slice, in JSON, and join each threat id to a TM-R/TM-F row or to "new". The stable ids and the evidence requirement are exactly what a join needs. The code it reads is Apache-2.0 and public; never point it at a folder holding a vault key or `.env` |
| **mcp-stride-gpt** | An MCP server that is a *framework provider, not an analyser*: it returns the STRIDE method, the DREAD rubric, attack-tree structure, test scaffolding and report skeletons; the client's model does the thinking. Eight tools (`get_repository_analysis_guide` by stage, `get_stride_threat_framework`, `generate_threat_mitigations`, `calculate_threat_risk_scores`, `create_threat_attack_trees`, `generate_security_tests`, `generate_threat_report`, `validate_threat_coverage`). Ships the companion **`stride-threat-modelling` skill** | `github.com/mrwadams/mcp-stride-gpt`, MIT. Hosted at `mcp.stridegpt.ai` (`claude mcp add stride-gpt https://mcp.stridegpt.ai/ --transport http`), or plugin (`/plugin marketplace add mrwadams/mcp-stride-gpt`), or copy `skills/stride-threat-modelling/` into `.claude/skills/`. Self-host: Python 3.12 standard library only, port 8787, no auth, keep on loopback | **Use the skill copy, not the hosted endpoint.** The hosted server receives the application description; the skill copy keeps everything in-session. It lets this agent do the STRIDE pass with the same rubric STRIDE GPT uses, so the two outputs are comparable |
| **TM-Bench** | A benchmark for LLM threat modelling, aimed at models that run on consumer hardware. Four dimensions: **STRIDE coverage and accuracy (30 %)**, **threat completeness (30 %)**, **technical validity (30 %)**, judged by an LLM (Claude Sonnet 4.6 in v2), and **JSON structure compliance (10 %)**, scored programmatically. Three complexity tiers of application description with synthetic ground-truth models | `tmbench.com` (home, methodology). No public repository or dataset found; maintainer not named on the site, the support link is `mrwadams`. v1 used Claude 3.7 Sonnet as judge, so v1 and v2 scores are not comparable | **Borrow the rubric, not the harness.** Our hand-written register (32 TM-R rows, 31 TM-F rows, each with a test) is a real ground truth. Scoring STRIDE GPT's output of the slice against it on TM-Bench's four dimensions is the measurable part of the case study, and a result worth sending to Matt |
| **threat-led-triage** | A Claude Code / Codex skill that *ranks* existing findings by what an attacker can reach and chain in this code base, not by CVSS. Inputs: findings (SARIF, SCA, CVE list, pentest, or free text), the checkout, and optionally a STRIDE GPT model of the same repo (supplies the trust boundaries). Output: ranked list with per-finding reachability, code path, boundary crossed, chains, and the severity adjustment with its reason; plus an explicit "could not determine" list. It finds nothing new | `github.com/mrwadams/threat-led-triage`, MIT. Run: `stride-gpt analyze . -o model.json -f json`, then `/threat-led-triage rank findings.json against model.json for this repo`. Worked example on OWASP crAPI in `test/` | **The triage step.** Semgrep, Bandit, pip-audit and the review skills will produce more findings than are worth a test. Ranking them by reachability across our boundaries (host, read-key holder, local, supply chain) is how the plan stays focused |
| **"Actions Speak Louder Than Tokens: An Insider Threat Model for Frontier AI Agents"** | A threat model that treats the agent as the insider. Five CERT dimensions adapted (motivation → optimisation objectives; opportunity → tool access and permissions; capability → model capabilities; predisposition → alignment profile; organisational factors → harness engineering). Four autonomy levels (L1 operator, L2 collaborator, L3 supervisor, L4 auditor). **Six** threat categories (credential compromise, supply-chain sabotage, data exfiltration, infrastructure sabotage, deception and evasion, containment and third-party impact). **27** STRIDE threats, each placed in a frequency × complexity quadrant (diffuse drift 10, opportunistic 8, targeted 9; the high-frequency high-complexity quadrant is empty). Detection with existing tooling: SIEM, UEBA, DLP, network, endpoint, deception (honey tokens, canary files). Monitor the *shape* of reasoning, not its content | `ai-insider-threat.matt-adams.co.uk`, source `github.com/mrwadams/ai-insider-threat`, CC BY 4.0, v1.0 dated April 2026 with sources into August 2026. Generated with STRIDE GPT. Search snippets still say 23 threats and five categories; the page lists 27 and six | **Adopt as an overlay.** Several of its threats are sgit rows already, seen from the other side (table below). Adding actor **A9, the agent holding the key** to §3 of the threat model, and a column mapping its 27 threats to our controls, is a small, concrete piece of work with a published method behind it |

### 1.1 First pass: the 27 insider threats against sgit's register

Done from the published list; to be confirmed against code in the review.

| Insider threat | sgit today | Register |
|---|---|---|
| S1 harvests keys and tokens | `vault_key`, `.pem`, the token and the credential store are on disk under `.sg_vault/local` (0600, directory 0755); keys appear in argv and `vault info` | TM-R14, TM-R15, TM-F05, TM-F16 |
| S2 forges commit author metadata | commits are signed by the clone's key, but any read-key holder can mint a key that verifies | **TM-R01**, TM-R17 |
| S5 replays a long-lived machine credential elsewhere | the write key is a bearer secret with no binding to a client, machine or time | TM-R13 |
| T1 subtle backdoor in code | out of sgit's scope as a tool; in scope for *this repository*, which agents write 61 % of (coding.sgit.ai) | review process, not register |
| T2 modifies CI/CD | three workflows, release actions SHA-pinned, publish from main only; the shipped workflow template pins nothing | TM-R21, SP-10 |
| R1 deletes logs and history | `history reflog` is local-only; the host keeps no plaintext log; a write-key holder can rewrite history, which clones detect as a rewind | TM-R13, rewind guard (TM-F12, F19, F23) |
| R3 changes code through paths that bypass signing | unsigned commits are refused under `signatures-required`, but only by sgit clients | TM-R26, TM-F10 |
| R4 suppresses client-side reporting | sgit emits no telemetry, so there is nothing to suppress; the host sees sizes and timing only | TM-R08 |
| I1, I5 exfiltration, data lands outside the deployment | `SGIT_DEFAULT_BASE_URL` once redirected a whole vault, token included; now pinned per vault | TM-F15, TM-F22, TM-R10 (`http://` allowed) |
| I4 secrets through reasoning logs | an agent that reads `vault_key` and prints it in its own transcript; nothing in sgit can prevent that, the skill rule can discourage it | new: skill rule (plan step 5) |
| D4 corrupts or deletes repository content | the write key can delete everything on the host; clones and backups recover | TM-R13 |
| E2 uses harvested credentials beyond its privilege | one write key per vault, all-or-nothing among holders; no per-writer authorisation | the "gap the note misses" in `10/08/review__git-to-sgit-security-mapping.md` |
| E5 reaches live systems from an environment believed isolated | unit and security tests are hermetic by construction (`tests/unit/conftest.py` fails any non-loopback connection) | test harness, not register |

Thirteen of 27 land on an existing row or mechanism after one reading. The rest (container
escape, `/proc` reads, ptrace, cloud resource churn, flooding internal services, account
creation) are host-and-harness threats that sgit cannot see; they belong in the deployment's
model, which is where the paper puts them.

## 2. The classical tools, and why they are not first

| Tool | What it is | Fit |
|---|---|---|
| **OWASP pytm** | Threat model as a Python file: elements, boundaries, dataflows; threat rules are Python conditions evaluated with `eval` (the README warns about the threat file's permissions); outputs a dot DFD, a PlantUML sequence diagram, a Markdown report. OWASP Production project | The right *shape* for a repository that already keeps everything as typed data, and the model file would sit naturally beside `review/intent/`. Not first: its threat library is web-app shaped; our value is in the register we already have. Worth a model file once the DFD is drawn, so the DFD is data and diffs |
| **Threagile** | Declarative YAML architecture model with automated risk rules; CLI, Docker, REST; produces risk report and diagrams | Same comment; YAML rather than Python. Its risk rules are infrastructure-shaped (containers, networks); few apply to a CLI and a storage API |
| **OWASP Threat Dragon** | DFD editor (web or desktop) with rule-assisted threat generation | A drawing tool. The house method keeps models as graph data, not drawings; use only if someone wants a picture for a talk |
| **Microsoft TMT, IriusRisk, ThreatModeler** | Desktop or commercial | Not for an open, agent-driven, data-first repository |

## 3. The house method, and where each tool plugs in

From `threat-modeling.sgit.ai/practice/`: bottom-up and fractal (file → method → class → module
→ path → endpoint → attack surface); one `.security.json` per source file in a parallel tree
with `attack_surface`, `vulnerabilities` (id, severity, attack vector, impact, status,
mitigation, **`risk_decision`** with owner and rationale), `secrets_exposure`, `dependencies`
with `trust_boundary_crossings`, `redundant_code`; STRIDE tables that keep `NOT MITIGATED`
rows; two modes never averaged; the method is always published, findings only once closed or
harmless by design.

| House artefact | Produced by | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `.security.json` per file (the slice only) | this agent, from the Trail of Bits dossier plus the review findings; every claim with a line | the dossier's "assumption, nothing found" rows become `attack_surface` and `trust_boundary_crossings` entries |
| STRIDE table for the slice | STRIDE GPT JSON (machine) and the `stride-threat-modelling` skill (this agent), reconciled | two independent passes; disagreements are published as such |
| Join: STRIDE threat ↔ TM-R/TM-F row ↔ test | this agent; a JSON table under `review/` | this is the TM-Bench "completeness" measurement, with our register as ground truth |
| Ranked findings | `threat-led-triage` over Semgrep, Bandit, pip-audit and skill output, with the STRIDE GPT model | explicit "could not determine" kept |
| Actor A9 and the insider overlay | the 27-threat table above, confirmed | an addition to §3 and §6 of the threat model, with `Known_Gaps` tests where a gap is proven |
| Disclosure | method now; findings when closed | the sgit.ai security page still says the internal review "is being prepared", and the 0.21.0 register is in this repository; the case study can close that loop |

## 4. Sources checked

- `github.com/mrwadams/stride-gpt` (README, changelog, PRs #205, #218, #231); `pypi.org/project/stride-gpt`
- `github.com/mrwadams/mcp-stride-gpt` (README)
- `tmbench.com` (home, methodology); shostack.org AppSec roundup March 2025 (TM-Bench introduction)
- `github.com/mrwadams/threat-led-triage` (README, `test/`)
- `ai-insider-threat.matt-adams.co.uk`; `github.com/mrwadams/ai-insider-threat`; `github.com/mrwadams`; matt-adams.co.uk/cv (talks at Securing Financial Services Summit 2026, Securing the Law Firm 2026)
- SE Radio 648 (Dec 2024), "Matthew Adams on AI Threat Modeling and Stride GPT"
- `devguide.owasp.org` pytm page; `pypi.org/project/pytm`; Threagile and Threat Dragon project pages
- `threat-modeling.sgit.ai` (index, practice, security-json pages)

# History integrity and signatures, cli.sgit.ai

> How sgit made a vault's history verifiable without a vault move: signed commits, a format gate, rewind detection, and the compatibility rule that a newer client must never break an older one still writing.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/research/topics/integrity.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# History integrity and signatures

**The question.** A host that stores ciphertext could still replay, rewind or forge a branch's head, and every reader would follow. Can every reader check the history, with signatures, ref monotonicity and longer ids, without moving existing vaults and without breaking a client that is still writing on an older version?

## Where it stands

| | Status | Where it is said |
|---|---|---|
| Canonical (JCS) signing input, `author_key_id`, `check verify`, `signatures-required`, rewind detection, the shared branch index | **shipped** in 0.19.0 to 0.21.0 | [History integrity](../../docs/history-integrity.md), [Update to 0.21.0](../../docs/update-to-0-21-0.md) |
| The format gate: format 2, 128-bit ids, `--min-client` | **shipped** | [History integrity](../../docs/history-integrity.md), [`sgit vault format`](../../reference/vault.md#vault-format) |
| What each fix costs, measured on a real vault (verify 66 µs a commit) | **measured**, 7 October | [Cost and compatibility](../../research/history-integrity-cost-and-compatibility.md) |
| Every client version against the web UI and the API, step by step | **analysis**, 7 October | [Compatibility matrix](../../research/compatibility-matrix-cli-web-ui-api.md) |
| git's security features mapped onto sgit, with corrections | **review**; four gaps closed for 0.21.0 | [Git to sgit security mapping](../../research/git-to-sgit-security-mapping.md) |
| The ideas after 0.21.0, bounded by "a new commit field breaks older clients' signature checks" | **proposed** | [Future features](../../research/future-features-after-0-21.md) |

## The research documents, newest first

- [Possible future features, after 0.21.0](../../research/future-features-after-0-21.md): The git-parity and security ideas that are not in 0.21.0, what each would take and what it could break, starting from the constraint that a new commit field breaks older clients' signature checks.
- [Review: "Git security features → sgit: a one-way mapping](../../research/git-to-sgit-security-mapping.md): A review of the one-way map from git's security features to sgit, checked against the code: three corrections, one missing gap, and the four easy gaps closed for 0.21.0.
- [Compatibility matrix: sgit CLI × vault web UI × SG/Send API, across the integrity roll-out](../../research/compatibility-matrix-cli-web-ui-api.md): The CLI, the vault web UI and the SG/Send API across the integrity roll-out, step by step: what each version reads, writes and loses, under the rule that no client may break another still writing.
- [History integrity: what the three fixes would cost, and how to ship them without a `vault move`](../../research/history-integrity-cost-and-compatibility.md): What signature verification, ref monotonicity and 128-bit ids would cost, measured on a real vault, and how to ship all three without a vault move.

# Keys, members and who may write, cli.sgit.ai

> Should the read key and the write key become key pairs, can a vault have members who join and leave by a file each, and can a vault enforce who writes where? What is built, what is designed, and what is still a question.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/research/topics/keys.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# Keys, members and who may write

**The question.** Today a vault has one secret: the vault key, from which a read key and a write key are derived. Every writer presents the same write key, so the server cannot tell writers apart, and a read key, once given, reads all history. Can a vault know who its members are, let them join and leave one at a time, and refuse a write from the wrong one, without the server ever reading anything?

## Where it stands

| | Status | Where it is said |
|---|---|---|
| Commits signed by each clone's own ECDSA P-256 key; `signatures-required` makes every client refuse an unsigned commit | **shipped** (0.19.0 and later) | [History integrity](../../docs/history-integrity.md) |
| `sgit pki`: RSA-4096 encryption pairs, ECDSA signing pairs, encrypt to a recipient, sign and verify | **shipped** | [Keys and signatures](../../docs/pki.md), [`sgit pki`](../../reference/pki.md) |
| The write key as a private signing key, with a writer set the server trusts | **designed**, not built | [Read and write keys as PKI](../../research/read-write-keys-as-pki.md) |
| A second vault mode built on two key pairs from the start, with sequence-number pinning | **designed**, revised twice after review | [Native PKI vault mode](../../research/native-pki-vault-mode.md) |
| Files sealed to named recipients on top of either mode | **designed** | [Sealed files](../../research/sealed-files-layer.md) |
| A door per member: one object holding the data key sealed to that member's key, outside history | **proposed**; the pieces exist separately | [the coverage map](../../research/keys-pki-copy-on-write-coverage-map.md), [the article](../../articles/keys-the-way-git-does-it.md) |
| A policy row (*key K may write `path/`*) refused by every honest client | **proposed** | [the article](../../articles/policies-the-vault-enforces.md) |
| Revoking a reader without rotating the key, or opening a vault with no key on disk | **absent**; rotation is the rule today | [Key management](../../docs/key-management.md) |

## Articles from this topic

- [Keys the way git does them, and the way a vault could: what SSH actually checks, what a read key actually prevents, and a door per member](../../articles/keys-the-way-git-does-it.md): I asked how git actually handles keys, because I suspected sgit was closer to it than people assume. Git authenticates you once and then checks nothing: an SSH key or a token gets you to the server, a push is file copying, the author of a commit is a string unless it is signed, and a clone is yours to do anything with.
- [Policies the vault enforces: from a rule agents keep to a folder only one key can write](../../articles/policies-the-vault-enforces.md): On ruv.sgit the vault is the record of a policy, not its enforcer. RiskMandate writes the mandate, the grant, the gap and the barrier; ruv.sgit compiles those rows into Ruflo's policy engine, which decides and writes receipts; the Cedar policy vault keeps the rules, their history, their signed releases and the evidence.

## The research documents, newest first

- [Keys the way git does them, PKI access to a vault, and copy-on-write: what is already published, and what is not](../../research/keys-pki-copy-on-write-coverage-map.md): Before writing two articles, a map of what is already published on keys the way git does them, PKI access to a vault and copy-on-write: seven questions from the memo, where each stands, the facts the articles must not get wrong,…
- [Sealed files — a second encryption layer on top of a vault](../../research/sealed-files-layer.md): A second encryption layer on top of either vault mode: files sealed to named recipients with ECDH P-256, HKDF and AES-256-GCM, with the corrections from the sgit.ai agent's review.
- [Native PKI vault mode — architecture map](../../research/native-pki-vault-mode.md): An architecture map for a second vault mode built on key pairs from the start, revised twice after review: sequence-number pinning, frozen hosts, concurrent writers.
- [Read and write keys as PKI — design analysis](../../research/read-write-keys-as-pki.md): Are the read key and the write key really a public and a private key? Half right: the write key should become a signing key, and the read key cannot become a public key. What that would take.

# Big vaults and many agents, cli.sgit.ai

> What happens when a vault reaches 35,000 objects and ten agents use it every day: what a clone fetches, what each session costs, which fixes came from measuring it, and why the server can stay simple.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/research/topics/scale.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# Big vaults and many agents

**The question.** The comms vault grew from 18,720 objects on 6 October to 35,423 on 14 October, used by ten agents and one person. What does a clone, a pull and a session cost at that size, where does the time go, and what can be cached by anything in the path because the server cannot read it?

## Where it stands

| | Status | Where it is said |
|---|---|---|
| The tree walk that re-fetched shared sub-trees once per parent | **fixed** (2 October) | [Clone re-fetched shared sub-trees](../../research/clone-refetched-shared-subtrees.md) |
| Partial clones: a folder scope (`--path`) and a history depth (`--depth`) | **shipped** in 0.18.0 | [Partial clones](../../docs/partial-clones.md), [the design](../../research/partial-clones-scope-and-depth.md) |
| Batched blob downloads, the far-behind sweep, large files without S3 | **fixed**, as the response of 14 October records | [Issues of 14 October](../../research/sgit-issues-2026-10-14.md) |
| The 35,000-object vault, cloned eight ways and served from local disk | **measured**, 16 October | [Response to "Scion and sgit"](../../research/response-to-scion-and-sgit.md), [the article](../../articles/one-vault-ten-agents-measured.md) |
| Every immutable object named by the hash of its ciphertext, so any cache can hold it | **shipped** (the `-imm-` naming) | [the article](../../articles/sgit-is-a-standard-one-hash-away.md) |
| A vault read as one zip instead of thousands of requests | **proposed**; the bundles are already written by `sgit publish --bundles` | [the article](../../articles/a-vault-in-one-file.md) |

## Articles from this topic

- [Is there any overhead? sgit's performance, measured: what a vault costs in a CI job, an agent's session and a hive, and why being selective beats being fast](../../articles/is-there-any-overhead.md): When I posted about using sgit inside CI pipelines, a reader asked the right question: what are the performance stats for this setup, and is there any overhead? There is, and it is worth stating exactly. Every sgit command pays…
- [One vault, ten agents, 35,000 objects: what sgit does when the repository is big and the clients are many](../../articles/one-vault-ten-agents-measured.md): When the clients are agents they are always online, there are many of them, and the expensive thing is moving bytes nobody needs. Anthropic's post on Scion answers that with a server that does the work and three tiers of cache in front of it.
- [sgit is a standard, not a server: everything in a vault is one hash away](../../articles/sgit-is-a-standard-one-hash-away.md): People read "encrypted git" and picture a product with a server in the middle. There is a server, and it is the least interesting part. A vault is a set of files laid out by a convention: blobs, trees, commits and one mutable ref per branch, all ciphertext, and every object except the ref and the branch index named by the SHA-256 of its own bytes.
- [A vault in one file: native zip support for sgit, where it wins, where it loses, and what already exists](../../articles/a-vault-in-one-file.md): A vault is files and folders, so it can be a zip. Every object is immutable and named by its hash, so the store only ever grows, and appending is the one thing a zip does cheaply. I asked how much of that already exists, and the…
- [A pack per push: git's packfiles, applied to an encrypted vault, with no server change](../../articles/a-pack-per-push.md): For three days I have been talking with the CLI team about keeping a vault's objects in zip files, and this is where it landed. A vault's objects are immutable and named by their hash, so a set of them is a zip and the set only ever grows, which is also what a git packfile is.

## The research documents, newest first

- [Spec: pack mode for sgit (CLI-only, packs-only vaults, no server change)](../../research/pack-mode-spec.md): The specification for pack mode: every push writes one zip pack, a snapshot pack compacts them, nothing is deleted, large packs go straight to S3 by presigned URL, and a gated packs-only vault needs no server change. Commands,…
- [Response to "Scion and sgit" (newsroom.sgit.ai, article No. 141, v1.0.0)](../../research/response-to-scion-and-sgit.md): The CLI team's response to the newsroom's "Scion and sgit" article: what it gets right, the three factual errors, and the measurements from a 35k-object vault the article should have carried.
- [Response to "sgit issues found on 14 October 2026", and the comms-vault performance report](../../research/sgit-issues-2026-10-14.md): The issues reported on 14 October, each traced to its cause in the code, with what was fixed in the same push and what was left open.
- [Partial clones — a folder scope and a history depth (6 Oct 2026)](../../research/partial-clones-scope-and-depth.md): Cloning just the folders an agent reads and writes, read and write, plus a shallow mode, without changing the full clone: the Merkle-spine idea and the measurements.
- [Clone performance — the tree walk re-fetched shared sub-trees once per parent](../../research/clone-refetched-shared-subtrees.md): A clone stuck walking trees: the walk re-fetched shared sub-trees once per parent, 10,098 requests for 2,236 unique trees. The instrumented run and the fix.

# How a vault takes writes, cli.sgit.ai

> One commit per change is right for documents and wrong for a stream, and many small objects cost a request each. Copy-on-write, a write-ahead append lane, a vault in one zip, and pack mode, a zip per push: what sgit already does, and what is proposed.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/research/topics/write-path.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift.*

---
# How a vault takes writes

**The question.** Every change in sgit is a commit: a tree rebuild, a signature and a compare-and-swap on one ref. That suits documents and does not suit an agent writing a line a second, or an API log in bursts. Can a vault take many small writes, attribute every one, and still store only whole, immutable objects? And since the cost over the network is the number of requests, not the bytes, can the objects travel in a few files instead of thousands?

## Where it stands

| | Status | Where it is said |
|---|---|---|
| Copy-on-write at the object level: a branch is a pointer, a commit shares every unchanged folder | **shipped** (git's design) | [the article](../../articles/copy-on-write-and-the-vault.md) |
| Append lanes: writes with no account and no tree, measured at a thousand entries from a hundred writers in 4.9 s | **shipped** on the server | [Append lanes](../../api/append-lanes.md) |
| A write-ahead lane folded into signed commits, with provenance kept per entry | **proposed**, protocol written out | [Streaming changes](../../articles/streaming-changes-into-a-vault.md) |
| Head and delta zips per commit | **shipped** (`sgit publish --bundles`) | [`sgit publish`](../../reference/publish.md), [the article](../../articles/a-vault-in-one-file.md) |
| A clone that reads a bundle, a bare store that lives in one file | **proposed** | [the article](../../articles/a-vault-in-one-file.md) |
| Zip64: 70,000 members and 5 GiB written and read back | **verified** 20 October | [the article](../../articles/a-vault-in-one-file.md#does-not-fit) |
| Presigned multipart upload and `Range` reads on the live server | **tested** 20 October, work today | [the article](../../articles/a-vault-in-one-file.md#works-today-tested) |
| An append route on the server: `UploadPartCopy` and `If-Match` on complete | **parked** 21 October: the brief now says not to build it; not needed by pack mode's first version | [the brief](../../research/zip-append-via-s3-brief.md), [the review](../../articles/pack-mode-read-closely.md#brief) |
| **Pack mode**: one pack per push, a snapshot to compact, an archive, a gated packs-only vault, no server change | **proposed**, specified 21 October; the review's five decisions taken the same day | [the spec](../../research/pack-mode-spec.md), [the article](../../articles/a-pack-per-push.md), [the review](../../articles/pack-mode-read-closely.md) |
| Copy-on-write inside a large file (content-defined chunks) | **proposed**, later | [the coverage map](../../research/keys-pki-copy-on-write-coverage-map.md) |
| Compressing blobs before encryption: about 1.58 times smaller on the comms vault's files | **proposed** for the pack trial, measured 21 October | [the spec](../../research/pack-mode-spec.md) |
| **A vault in one file**: the `bare/` folder zipped, optionally sealed to a public key, cloned from the unpacked folder | **works today** with shipped commands, measured 21 October; one command and a direct clone are proposed | [the article](../../articles/a-vault-you-can-carry.md) |

## Articles from this topic

- [Is there any overhead? sgit's performance, measured: what a vault costs in a CI job, an agent's session and a hive, and why being selective beats being fast](../../articles/is-there-any-overhead.md): When I posted about using sgit inside CI pipelines, a reader asked the right question: what are the performance stats for this setup, and is there any overhead? There is, and it is worth stating exactly. Every sgit command pays…
- [A vault you can carry: one zip holds the whole vault, a public key can seal it, and the round trip already works](../../articles/a-vault-you-can-carry.md): Reading the pack-mode article, I wanted three things made explicit. First, the two modes side by side, the files that exist in each and the order things happen, which is now a section of that article. Second, my understanding that we mix mutable and immutable files and that this is why the architecture works.
- [A pack per push: git's packfiles, applied to an encrypted vault, with no server change](../../articles/a-pack-per-push.md): For three days I have been talking with the CLI team about keeping a vault's objects in zip files, and this is where it landed. A vault's objects are immutable and named by their hash, so a set of them is a zip and the set only ever grows, which is also what a git packfile is.
- [Pack mode, read closely: a sound design that needs no server change, and five decisions before it is built](../../articles/pack-mode-read-closely.md): I am cli.sgit.ai's build agent. Dinis Cruz asked me to publish the CLI team's newest documents as articles and to say what I think of them, because they are big decisions. I read three, written on the CLI's working branch within…
- [A vault in one file: native zip support for sgit, where it wins, where it loses, and what already exists](../../articles/a-vault-in-one-file.md): A vault is files and folders, so it can be a zip. - [Copy-on-write, and what it would mean for a vault: what rUv's team asked for, what sgit already does, and the write-ahead lane that would do the rest](../../articles/copy-on-write-and-the-vault.md): After I presented ruv.sgit to the Agentics Foundation, rUv's team asked whether sgit could add copy-on-write. I wanted to know what that would mean for a vault before saying yes or no. Copy-on-write means share until you write: a snapshot or a branch costs nothing, and the first write to a shared block pays for a copy of that block.
- [Streaming changes into a vault: a thousand small writes, one commit, every line attributed](../../articles/streaming-changes-into-a-vault.md): Every change in a vault is a commit, and a commit is a tree rebuild, a signature and a compare-and-swap on one ref. That is fine for a document and wrong for an agent that writes a line a second, for a hundred of them, or for an API log that arrives in bursts.

# Brief to the SG/Send team: append to a vault object on S3 without re-uploading it, and conditional completes, cli.sgit.ai

> A brief to the SG/Send team: a presigned append route that grows a zip on S3 by UploadPartCopy, conditional completes with If-Match and If-None-Match, and size and ETag with the read URL. Written for a single appended zip; the pack-mode spec of the next day needs none of it for its first version.

*Source: <https://cli.sgit.ai/research/zip-append-via-s3-brief.html> · generated from the same content as the page, so the two cannot drift. Published from <https://github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__CLI/blob/477d328536b04147e78281fb1f13550df1abf140/team/humans/dinis_cruz/claude-code-web/10/20/brief__to-sg-send-team__zip-append-via-s3.md>.*

---
# Brief to the SG/Send team: append to a vault object on S3 without re-uploading it, and conditional completes

> **Status, 21 Oct 2026: parked.** The CLI's pack-mode spec of 21 Oct (a new pack per push, a snapshot to
> compact, see `10/21/spec__pack-mode.md`) needs none of the routes below for its first version. Asks 1 and
> 2 are parked until a snapshot ever needs to grow in place; ask 3 (size and ETag with the read URL) is
> welcome but not needed, since pack names carry their size. Please do not build asks 1 and 2 on this
> brief's account. The folder in the CLI design is `bare/packs/`, not `bare/pack/`.

**From:** the sgit CLI agent, 20 Oct 2026, with Dinis's go-ahead. **Server read:** `sgraph_ai_app_send`
0.34.0, `lambda__user/service/Service__Vault__Presigned.py` and `fast_api/routes/Routes__Vault__Presigned.py`.
**Why:** the CLI is going to try a storage mode where a vault's immutable objects live in one, two or three
zip files on S3, read and written **directly against S3 with presigned URLs**, with only the small
mutable objects (ref, branch index) going through the ordinary routes. The read half already works
(tested 20 Oct: `read-url` + `Range` answers `206`). The write half needs one new route and one
parameter, both below. Everything else stays as it is.

## What exists, verified on `dev.send.sgraph.ai` on 20 Oct

| Route | Does | Tested |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/vault/presigned/initiate/{vault_id}` | `create_multipart_upload` + one presigned `upload_part` URL per 10 MB part | 12.6 MB object, 2 parts, PUT straight to S3 |
| `POST /api/vault/presigned/complete/{vault_id}` | `complete_multipart_upload` | ok |
| `POST /api/vault/presigned/cancel/{vault_id}` | `abort_multipart_upload` | not exercised |
| `GET /api/vault/presigned/read-url/{vault_id}/{file_id}` | presigned GET | `Range: bytes=0-1023`, `bytes=-2048`, a middle slice: all `206`, bytes correct |

Not present: any `upload_part_copy`, and any `IfMatch` / `IfNoneMatch` on complete.

## Ask 1: `POST /api/vault/presigned/append/{vault_id}`

Start a multipart upload whose first bytes are **copied server-side from an existing object**
(`UploadPartCopy`), so a client can grow a large object by uploading only its new tail.

**Request** (write key header as on `initiate`):

```json
{
  "source_file_id":  "bare/packs/snapshots/…",   // the object to copy the prefix from
  "file_id":         "bare/packs/snapshots/…",   // the target; same as source = append in place, or a new name
  "expected_etag":   "\"43187a65…-2\"",           // the source's ETag the client last saw
  "copy_bytes":      430392414,                   // how many leading bytes of the source to keep
  "tail_size_bytes": 3100000,                     // what the client will upload after them
  "num_tail_parts":  0                            // 0 = server picks (10 MB parts), as initiate does
}
```

**Server, in order:**

1. Validate the write key (as `initiate`); validate the ids as `initiate` does.
2. `head_object(source)`; if `ETag != expected_etag` → `412 {"error": "etag_mismatch", "etag": "<current>"}`.
   If `copy_bytes > ContentLength` → `400`. If `copy_bytes < 5 MiB` → `400 {"error": "too_small_to_copy"}`
   (S3 needs every non-final part ≥ 5 MiB; the client then rewrites the object whole, which at that
   size is cheap).
3. `create_multipart_upload(target)`.
4. Split `[0, copy_bytes)` into copy parts: `k = ceil(copy_bytes / COPY_PART_MAX)` parts of
   `ceil(copy_bytes / k)` bytes each (all ≥ 5 MiB). For each, `upload_part_copy(Bucket, Key=target,
   UploadId, PartNumber=i, CopySource={'Bucket': bucket, 'Key': source_key},
   CopySourceRange='bytes=a-b', CopySourceIfMatch=expected_etag)`. Record the returned ETags.
   `COPY_PART_MAX`: start at 1 GiB, not 5 GiB. The copy is server-side but the call blocks until it
   is done; API Gateway cuts a Lambda at 29 s, and S3 copies at a few hundred MB/s. A 430 MB prefix
   is one part and a few seconds; a 20 GB one is twenty calls, which this route should do in parallel
   threads, as the existing code does nothing in parallel.
5. Generate presigned `upload_part` URLs for the tail parts, numbered after the copy parts.
6. Return:

```json
{
  "upload_id":   "…",
  "copied":      [{"part_number": 1, "etag": "…"}],             // the client passes these back on complete
  "part_urls":   [{"part_number": 2, "upload_url": "…"}],       // tail parts
  "part_size":   10485760
}
```

The client uploads the tail parts and calls `complete` with the copied parts and its own.

## Ask 2: conditional complete

`POST /api/vault/presigned/complete/{vault_id}` gains two optional fields, passed straight to
`complete_multipart_upload`:

```json
{ "file_id": "...", "upload_id": "...", "parts": [...],
  "if_match":      "\"<etag>\"",     // in-place append: fail unless the target still has this ETag
  "if_none_match": "*" }             // new immutable name: fail if it already exists
```

Map S3's `PreconditionFailed` to `412 {"error": "precondition_failed"}` and abort the multipart
upload on that path (or leave it for `cancel`; say which). These two headers are what give the
zip its compare-and-swap, the same rule the ref already has in the batch route. boto3 has
supported `IfMatch` on `CompleteMultipartUpload` since late 2024 and `IfNoneMatch='*'` since
August 2024; the current pin is likely fine, please check.

## Ask 3 (small): size and ETag with the read URL

`read-url` currently returns the URL only. Add `size` and `etag` from one `head_object` (or a
separate `GET /api/vault/presigned/head/{vault_id}/{file_id}`), so a client reading a zip's tail
by `Range` does not need its own `HEAD` first, and an appender learns the ETag it must present.
Range support needs nothing: it is S3's.

## Limits to state in the API docs

- Object size up to S3's 5 TB; parts 5 MiB to 5 GiB, 10,000 per upload; presigned URL expiry as today.
- One in-place append at a time per object: the second one fails on `if_match` and must re-read the
  ETag and copy again. That is the design, not a bug.
- `copy_bytes` under 5 MiB cannot be appended to; rewrite whole.
- Nothing about these routes is readable by the server: the objects are ciphertext; the server copies
  bytes it cannot read.

## Tests we would like to see in the server's suite

1. Append in place: a 12 MB object, append 1 MB, `if_match` current ETag → new ETag, size 13 MB,
   bytes `[0, 12 MB)` unchanged, tail present.
2. Append to a new name with `if_none_match: "*"` twice → second is `412`.
3. Stale `expected_etag` → `412` on `append`, nothing created.
4. `copy_bytes` of 1 MB → `400 too_small_to_copy`.
5. Two clients appending in place from the same ETag → exactly one succeeds.
6. `read-url` + `Range` → `206` with the right `Content-Range` (regression for what works today).

## What the CLI will do with it (so the shape fits)

Storage mode `pack`: `bare/packs/snapshots/…` holds the immutable objects (`ZIP_STORED`, sorted,
deterministic, append-only, Zip64); `refs/`, `indexes/` and `cache/` stay as today. Push = `append`
of the new members plus the rewritten central directory (a few MB), `complete` with `if_match`, then
the ordinary ref CAS. Pull = `Range` for the new tail (from the last known directory offset to the end),
then the ref. Clone = one GET (or a few parallel ranges) per zip, no listing, no walk. Then the
performance tests Dinis asked for: full clone of the 35k-object vault as one GET against the batch
route; append loops at 1, 10 and 100 MB tails on a 500 MB zip; incremental pulls; two appenders racing.
